root_cause: In _partition_base_optimizer_state, the alignment used for re-flattening merged optimizer state was just dist.get_world_size(group), but ZeRO pads optimizer states by nccl_start_alignment_factor * world_size when saving. invariant: After load_checkpoint, optimizer.state[p] tensors must equal the pre-save optimizer.state[p] tensors element-wise for every parameter p.
title: ZeRO 1/2 elastic checkpoint optimizer state alignment ignores nccl_start_alignment_factor
diff_summary: Multiply alignment by self.nccl_start_alignment_factor in _partition_base_optimizer_state when re-partitioning merged optimizer states.

root_cause: In refactor PR #4695, allreduce_bucket(self, bucket, rank=None, ...) was added with a hard `rank = None` reset at the very top of the function, which silently overrides any rank passed in by callers. The intended single-destination reduce path is therefore never taken and gradients always go through allreduce, producing different numerics on the receiving rank than expected.
invariant: When use_multi_rank_bucket_allreduce is False, dist.reduce should be called for gradient buckets while dist.all_reduce should not.
title: ZeRO2 allreduce_bucket forces rank=None, never uses single-rank reduce path
diff_summary: Remove the hard-coded `rank = None` line at the top of allreduce_bucket so that the caller-supplied rank is honored.

root_cause: The decision to copy a parameter's gradient into the contiguous IPG bucket used a strict less-than comparison (`elements_in_ipg_bucket + param.grad.numel() < reduce_bucket_size`). When a param exactly fills the remaining bucket capacity the branch was skipped, so the gradient was never copied into the contiguous buffer and never reduced — the parameter silently received a stale (or zero) gradient.
invariant: For every trainable param p with non-None grad after backward, the reduced gradient on the owning rank must be non-zero (or, when expected to be zero, must equal the locally computed grad).
title: ZeRO3 contiguous_gradients off-by-one — last param exactly filling bucket is dropped
diff_summary: Change `<` to `<=` in the contiguous_gradients bucket-fit check in DeepSpeedZeroOptimizer_Stage3.reduce_independent_p_g_buckets_and_remove_grads.

root_cause: Two bugs together: (1) load_zero_checkpoint required load_optimizer_states even when only loading the bf16 module, so it ran with no checkpoint files; (2) inside _load_checkpoint, the call to optimizer.refresh_fp32_params() was guarded by self.fp16_enabled(), so for bf16 the high-precision master weights were never refreshed from the loaded 16-bit module. Training proceeds with default-initialized fp32 master weights.
invariant: After load_checkpoint with load_module_only=True, optimizer.fp32_groups_flat[i] must equal bf16_groups_flat[i].float() for every group i.
title: load_module_only with bf16 silently skips refresh_fp32_params, optimizer trains on uninitialized fp32 weights
diff_summary: Drop the load_optimizer_states gate on load_zero_checkpoint and drop the fp16_enabled() gate on optimizer.refresh_fp32_params() so bf16 also refreshes its master copy.

root_cause: In zero.Init.__init__, when the deepspeed config has zero_quantized_nontrainable_weights=True but the local kwarg is False, the code mistakenly assigns the value to self.quantized_weights instead of self.quantized_nontrainable_weights — a copy-paste typo. Trainable weights end up being quantized while the nontrainable weights stay full precision (the opposite of what was requested).
trigger_conditions: constructor caller did not pass zero_quantized_nontrainable_weights explicitly
invariant: After zero.Init, self.quantized_nontrainable_weights must equal config.zero_quantized_nontrainable_weights.
title: ZeRO3 quantized_nontrainable_weights flag overwrites quantized_weights instead
diff_summary: Replace `self.quantized_weights = ...` with `self.quantized_nontrainable_weights = ...` on the misassigned line.

root_cause: In __avg_scatter_contiguous_grads the gate was `if self.communication_data_type == self.dtype:` — exactly backward. When the user requested a different communication dtype, the buffer was NOT cast, so reduce-scatter ran on the wrong dtype; when it matched the model dtype the code wastefully cast to itself.
trigger_conditions: communication_data_type != model dtype (e.g. fp32 comm with bf16 model)
invariant: Inside __avg_scatter_contiguous_grads the tensor passed to reduce_scatter must have dtype == self.communication_data_type.
title: ZeRO3 communication_data_type comparison inverted — buffer cast happens only when no cast is needed
diff_summary: Flip the condition from `self.communication_data_type == self.dtype` to `self.communication_data_type != dtype` so the cast happens exactly when needed.

root_cause: Two related bugs: (a) The dtype dispatch picked the BFLOAT16 optimizer path for bf16+fp32-grad-accum even when CPU offload was on, where it doesn't work correctly. (b) For an extra-large param the reduction code took `self.extra_large_param_to_reduce.grad` directly instead of routing through get_gradient_for_reduction(), so when use_grad_accum_for_reduction was on the accumulated fp32 grad was bypassed and the raw bf16 grad was reduced (loss of precision and stale value).
invariant: When use_grad_accum_for_reduction is True, the tensor passed to average_tensor must be the same object/dtype as get_gradient_for_reduction(param), not param.grad.
title: bf16+ZeRO1+CPU offload silently routes through bf16 wrapper; extra-large param uses raw param.grad instead of reduction grad
diff_summary: Add `and not self.zero_cpu_offload()` to the BFLOAT16 path selection, route extra-large param reduction through get_gradient_for_reduction, and copy from grad_reduc instead of param.grad in the contiguous bucket path.

root_cause: After optimizer.step(), the loop that copies fp32 master weights back to bf16/fp16 partitions used a single `partition_id` taken from the outer scope. With MoE, different param groups use different real_dp_process_group with different ranks, so the wrong partition slot in bit16_partitions was overwritten and the local rank's actual partition was never updated.
trigger_conditions: MoE model with expert parallel groups != data parallel group
invariant: After optimizer.step, bit16_partitions[i][rank_i_in_group] must equal single_partition_of_fp32_groups[i].to(bit16_dtype) for every group i, where rank_i_in_group = dist.get_rank(group=real_dp_process_group[i]).
title: ZeRO2 + MoE: fp32→fp16 master-weight copy uses outer-loop partition_id, writing into wrong rank's slice
diff_summary: Compute partition_id per group inside the zip loop using dist.get_rank(group=real_dp_process_group[group_id]) instead of reusing the outer-scope value.

expected_output.buggy: BUG DETECTED

invariant: Optimizer groups must only contain params with requires_grad=True
title: Frozen parameters included in optimizer groups

root_cause: When building bit16_param_groups for DeepSpeedCPUAdam.step(fp16_param_groups=...) and when copying fp32 partitions back to bit16 partitions, the code used a single outer-scope partition_id for all groups instead of computing the rank within each group's real_dp_process_group. With more than one group, every group except the first received the wrong rank's partition.
trigger_conditions: multiple param groups using different real_dp_process_group
invariant: For each ZeRO param group i, the bit16 partition that was updated by DeepSpeedCPUAdam must be bit16_partitions[i][dist.get_rank(real_dp_process_group[i])].
title: ZeRO2 + CPU offload: DeepSpeedCPUAdam fp32→fp16 partition_id is wrong across param groups
diff_summary: Compute partition_id per group via dist.get_rank(real_dp_process_group[group_id]) inside the bit16_param_groups list comprehension and inside the post-step copy loop.

root_cause: The bookkeeping loop that builds param_to_partition_ids/is_partition_reduced iterated over self.fp16_groups (the original parameter order) even though gradient reduction itself uses self.round_robin_fp16_groups (the reordered list). The partition-owner table therefore disagreed with the actual reduction destination, so some params' gradients were attributed to the wrong owner and never appeared in the optimizer step.
invariant: param_to_partition_ids must be built from the same parameter ordering that average_tensor / reduce_scatter uses (round_robin_fp16_groups when round_robin_gradients is enabled).
title: ZeRO2 round-robin gradient partitioning uses non-reordered group, mapping params to wrong partition owner
diff_summary: Iterate over self.round_robin_fp16_groups instead of self.fp16_groups when populating partition bookkeeping tables in stage2.

root_cause: ds_utils.partition_balanced used a binary-search probe (_lprobe / _rb_partition_balanced) that, when probed with uniform weights, returned a non-monotone boundary list like [0,2,4,5,5] for 5 items / 4 parts — i.e. the last stage owns 0 layers. Pipeline modules construct from that boundary list and silently train with a stage holding no parameters.
trigger_conditions: uniform layer weights (e.g. partition by parameter count of identical layers)
invariant: For every adjacent pair (parts[p], parts[p+1]) returned by partition_balanced, parts[p+1] - parts[p] must be >= 1 (each PP stage owns at least one item).
title: Pipeline partition_balanced returns degenerate partitions, last PP stage can be assigned zero layers
diff_summary: Replace the binary-search _rb_partition_balanced with a direct cumulative-weight greedy partitioner that guarantees every part receives at least one item.

root_cause: self.save_non_zero_checkpoint = (rank == 0) or zero_optimization_partition_weights() became True for every MiCS rank because zero_optimization_partition_weights() is True under MiCS. All ranks then wrote the consolidated non-ZeRO checkpoint file, racing with each other and silently leaving inconsistent contents on disk.
invariant: For a MiCS run with shard_size S, exactly S ranks (those with global_rank < S) should report save_non_zero_checkpoint=True; all other ranks should report False.
title: MiCS save_non_zero_checkpoint True on every rank — checkpoint files race-overwrite each other
diff_summary: Add is_first_weights_partition_group() helper and AND it with zero_optimization_partition_weights() when computing save_non_zero_checkpoint.

root_cause: all_gather_coalesced built one flat partition buffer assuming a single ds_tensor dtype across all params in the group, so when the param list contained mixed dtypes the larger-dtype params were silently truncated/aliased into the smaller-dtype buffer. After allgather, parameters held garbage bit patterns until the next iteration overwrote them.
trigger_conditions: model contains parameters of more than one floating dtype (e.g. fp32 LayerNorm + bf16 weights)
invariant: After all_gather_coalesced, every gathered param p must satisfy p.data.dtype == p.ds_tensor.dtype and p.numel() * p.element_size() bytes were transferred for p.
title: ZeRO3 allgather hardcodes ds_tensor dtype — mixed-dtype param groups silently allgather wrong bytes
diff_summary: Group params by dtype before allgather and issue one allgather per dtype with a per-dtype flat buffer.

root_cause: The training and eval PartitionedParameterCoordinators were both constructed with the same shared InflightParamRegistry. When the engine switched modes, in-flight allgather handles registered under one coordinator were observed by the other, which would either re-issue allgather on a still-inflight param or wait on a handle that was never going to fire — leading to silently-stale parameter values during the first iteration after the switch.
invariant: Each PartitionedParameterCoordinator must own a private InflightParamRegistry; the registry instance held by the train coordinator must not be the same Python object as the eval coordinator's.
title: ZeRO3 InflightParamRegistry shared between train and eval coordinators causes stale handles on mode switch
diff_summary: Replace the single module-level registry with a {True: InflightParamRegistry(), False: InflightParamRegistry()} dict keyed by training flag, and pass the per-mode registry to each coordinator.

root_cause: In DeepSpeedZeroOptimizer.step, _global_grad_norm was computed as scaled_global_grad_norm / self.loss_scale. But self.loss_scale is the *new* scale (already updated for this step), while the gradients that produced scaled_global_grad_norm were scaled by the *previous* scale (prev_scale). Dividing by the wrong scale silently skews the global grad norm used for clipping.
trigger_conditions: step where loss_scale was just halved due to overflow / scale-window
invariant: self._global_grad_norm * prev_scale must equal scaled_global_grad_norm for the step (i.e. unscaling uses the same factor that backward applied).
title: ZeRO step uses post-decay loss_scale to unscale grad norm instead of prev_scale used during backward
diff_summary: Divide scaled_global_grad_norm by prev_scale (captured before the loss-scale update) instead of self.loss_scale.

root_cause: In _get_gradients_for_reduction, the sparse-gradient branch wrapped `param.grad.data` into a SparseTensor: `grad_data = SparseTensor(grad_data)`. Because Python re-bound the local name and never wrote back into param.grad, the post-allreduce updated values were stored on a temporary SparseTensor that had no link to the parameter — the sparse embedding gradients were silently dropped.
invariant: After buffered_allreduce_fallback, param.grad of a sparse-gradient parameter must reflect the all-reduced values (non-zero where local grad was non-zero).
title: Sparse gradients silently not updating — SparseTensor wraps .data instead of param.grad
diff_summary: Construct SparseTensor from param.grad (not param.grad.data) so the SparseTensor wrapper retains a write path back to the parameter.

root_cause: In _aggregate_total_loss the last stage built `losses = torch.stack([self.dp_group_loss, agg_loss])` and broadcast it to other PP stages. When the source tensors were bf16 the broadcast tensor was bf16 too, but other ranks initialised their receive buffer as fp32 (default Tensor()), so dist.broadcast wrote bf16 bytes into an fp32 tensor and other PP stages saw garbage scalar losses.
invariant: After dist.broadcast inside _aggregate_total_loss, the losses tensor must have the same dtype on every PP rank.
title: Pipeline parallel _aggregate_total_loss broadcasts torch.stack of mixed-dtype losses, non-last stages receive wrong dtype
diff_summary: Force losses to fp32 with `.float()` on the last stage before the broadcast so all PP ranks agree on dtype.

root_cause: zero_wrapper_for_fp_tensor_constructor cast tensors to the target dtype with `tensor = tensor.to(target_fp_dtype)`. For tensors that were already nn.Parameter (or had requires_grad=True), .to() returns a fresh non-Parameter Tensor without the autograd hook; the wrapper rebound the local name but the model still held the original reference, so the model's Parameter kept the wrong dtype and the (correctly-cast) shadow tensor became unreachable.
trigger_conditions: model code constructs a tensor with requires_grad=True (e.g. via torch.empty(...).requires_grad_(True))
invariant: After zero.Init wraps a tensor constructor, the tensor visible to the model must satisfy `tensor.dtype == target_fp_dtype` and remain the same Python object that the model references.
title: ZeRO param dtype cast inside zero_wrapper_for_fp_tensor_constructor reassigns Parameter to a non-Parameter Tensor
diff_summary: Cast in-place via `tensor.data = tensor.data.to(target_fp_dtype)` so the original Parameter object is preserved and its dtype actually changes.

root_cause: ZeRO3's checkpoint logic only iterated trainable parameters when assembling the per-rank state and the zero_to_fp32 reconstruction script. Frozen parameters were never written to the checkpoint at all, so resuming with a fresh model whose frozen tensors are random-initialised silently trains from corrupted weights with no warning.
trigger_conditions: model has parameters with requires_grad=False (e.g. frozen embedding, LoRA-tuned model)
invariant: For every nn.Parameter p in module.named_parameters(), the saved checkpoint must contain a tensor or fragment whose name matches p (regardless of p.requires_grad).
title: ZeRO3 checkpoint silently omits frozen (requires_grad=False) parameters from saved state
diff_summary: Add FROZEN_PARAM_SHAPES / FROZEN_PARAM_FRAGMENTS to checkpoint constants, save frozen params as separate fragments in BF16/ZeRO3 checkpoints, and extend zero_to_fp32 to merge them back.

root_cause: DeepSpeedZeroOptimizer_Stage3._setup_for_real_optimizer called _create_fp16_partitions_with_defragmentation() on the raw self.optimizer.param_groups, including frozen params. Frozen params became part of the partitioned trainable list — they were placed into Adam fp32 state and received update increments from optimizer.step, silently un-freezing them.
invariant: Across optimizer steps, p.data must remain unchanged for every nn.Parameter with requires_grad=False.
title: ZeRO3 builds fp16 partitions from full param_groups including frozen params, OOM-equivalent silent waste plus unused optimizer state
diff_summary: Add _get_trainable_parameter_groups() that filters by requires_grad and pass the filtered list into _create_fp16_partitions_with_defragmentation.

root_cause: _save_moe_checkpoint short-circuited with `if exp_dp_rank != 0: return` before saving the per-mp-rank model_states.pt files. With TP > 1, only the rank that was both expert-DP-zero and mp-rank-zero ever wrote model_states.pt; all other TP shards were skipped, so resuming silently loaded mp_rank_00 onto every TP rank, training all TP ranks with the same shard.
invariant: After save_checkpoint with MoE+TP, exactly one mp_rank_XX_model_states.pt must exist for every X in [0, tp_world_size).
title: MOE save_checkpoint with TP > 1 only writes mp_rank_00_model_states.pt — non-zero TP ranks lose non-MoE weights
diff_summary: Restructure the early-return so non-MoE-state writing (model_states.pt) still runs on data_parallel_rank == 0 even when exp_dp_rank != 0.

root_cause: create_reduce_and_remove_grad_hooks built the per-param backward hook via `wrapper(param, i)` where `i` was the loop index over groups. Because `i` was Python-late-bound inside the closure, every hook fired with the same final value of `i`, routing earlier groups' gradients into the last group's reduction bucket. The fix removes the unused `i` argument entirely (the bucket is determined from the param itself).
invariant: For every backward hook registered for parameter p in group i, the hook must call reduce_independent_p_g_buckets_and_remove_grads(p) without binding to a stale group index.
title: ZeRO3 backward hook closure captures stale group index `i` — gradient routed to wrong reduction bucket
diff_summary: Drop the unused `i` parameter from wrapper / reduce_independent_p_g_buckets_and_remove_grads / reduce_ready_partitions_and_remove_grads in stage3.py.

root_cause: All ZeRO/BF16 wrappers eagerly called the inner optimizer's step() during construction in order to materialize state tensors. This silently incremented the Adam state[`step`] counter for every param before any real backward pass, so the bias-correction terms were off by one (and beta1^t / beta2^t for the first few real steps were wrong) compared to vanilla PyTorch.
invariant: Right after deepspeed.initialize, optimizer.state[p]['step'] must equal 0 for every parameter p (no fake step has run).
title: ZeRO optimizer.step() called once during initialization, increments Adam step counter before any real update
diff_summary: Replace the eager optimizer.step() in initialization with a lazy_init_hp_params_optimizer_state hook that runs after the first real step to link hp params to optimizer state.

root_cause: When grad_accum_dtype was unspecified, the engine auto-selected fp32 for any bf16 model. Under ZeRO this is silently wrong because ZeRO assumes grad_accum_dtype == model_dtype; gradient accumulation buffers ended up in fp32 while reduction ran in bf16, so accumulated gradients were lost on the first cast back.
invariant: When ZeRO is enabled and grad_accum_dtype is not user-set, grad_accum_dtype must equal model_dtype.
title: BF16 model + ZeRO defaults silently force fp32 grad accum buffer despite ZeRO requiring matching dtype
diff_summary: Add `and not self.zero_optimization()` to the auto-promotion-to-fp32 branch so ZeRO+bf16 keeps grad_accum_dtype = bf16 by default.

root_cause: DeepSpeedEngine.allreduce_gradients drove ZeRO's overlapping_partition_gradients_reduce_epilogue, but never told the optimizer whether the engine was at a real GAS boundary. ZeRO's internal `is_gradient_accumulation_boundary` therefore stayed at its default and reduction kicked off on every micro-batch, silently destroying accumulation correctness for PP+ZeRO.
invariant: self.optimizer.is_gradient_accumulation_boundary must equal engine.is_gradient_accumulation_boundary() at the entry of allreduce_gradients (one True per GAS, GAS-1 Falses).
title: Pipeline + ZeRO: gradient accumulation boundary flag never propagated, ZeRO does early reduction every micro-step
diff_summary: In allreduce_gradients, set self.optimizer.is_gradient_accumulation_boundary = self.is_gradient_accumulation_boundary() before invoking ZeRO's reduce epilogue.

root_cause: DeepSpeedDataLoader.__init__ set self.len = len(self.data_sampler), the count of underlying samples. Callers using len(dataloader) (e.g. lr scheduler total_num_steps, progress bars, max_steps detection) silently received the sample count instead of the batch count, off by ~batch_size× — schedules and step counters silently drift.
invariant: len(DeepSpeedDataLoader) must equal len(sampler)//batch_size when drop_last=True, else ceil(len(sampler)/batch_size).
title: DeepSpeedDataLoader.len reports sampler length, ignores batch_size and drop_last
diff_summary: Compute self.len from len(self.data_sampler)/batch_size (floor or ceil depending on dataloader_drop_last).

root_cause: BF16_Optimizer ignored the requested grad_acc_dtype and always allocated `fp32_groups_gradients_flat` as fp32. When the user explicitly requested bf16 grad accumulation (to save memory) the buffer dtype mismatched the configured dtype, the engine reported wrong memory usage, and the param_partition.grad cast at step time silently down-cast accumulated values losing precision in an unexpected place.
invariant: BF16_Optimizer.fp32_groups_gradients_flat[i].dtype must equal the configured grad_acc_dtype.
title: BF16_Optimizer fp32 grad accumulator allocated as fp32 even when grad_acc_dtype is bf16
diff_summary: Plumb grad_acc_dtype into BF16_Optimizer constructor, allocate the grad-accum flat buffer with that dtype, and cast to fp32 only at step time when needed.

root_cause: reduce_independent_p_g_buckets_and_remove_grads set `self.extra_large_param_to_reduce = param` whenever a param exceeded reduce_bucket_size, regardless of contiguous_gradients. With contiguous_gradients=False the IPG buffer path is never taken, so the assignment was a dead store but the reference outlived the iteration. On the next backward pass the ipg-flush code saw the stale extra_large_param_to_reduce and called average_tensor on a previous-iteration gradient (silent corruption).
invariant: self.extra_large_param_to_reduce must be None (or never set) when self.contiguous_gradients is False.
title: ZeRO2 extra_large_param leaks reference when contiguous_gradients=False — silent stale-grad reduction in next step
diff_summary: Wrap the extra_large_param_to_reduce assignment and the contiguous-buffer copy inside `if self.contiguous_gradients:` so neither runs when the feature is disabled.

root_cause: AutoEP runs one logical batch across an EP group (each EP rank sees a slice of tokens), so each rank's scalar loss is only 1/ep_size of the logical-batch loss. The buggy DeepSpeedEngine.backward() does not multiply the loss by ep_size before backward, so reduced expert gradients end up scaled by 1/ep_size relative to the equivalent ZeRO-2 / ep_size=1 baseline. Optimizer.step then applies effectively-shrunk gradients, biasing every step.
invariant: For matched (DP=N, EP=1) vs (DP=N/ep, EP=ep) AutoEP runs with identical logical batch and seed, post-step expert weights must be approximately equal (within fp32 tolerance).
title: AutoEP ZeRO-2 forgets to scale per-rank loss by EP-group size — expert gradients undercount by factor ep_size
diff_summary: Compute self._autoep_output_grad_scale = ep_world_size in _configure_distributed_model; in backward() multiply loss and gas_scaled_loss by this factor before optimizer.backward().
silent_check: Buggy code feeds an unmodified (smaller) loss tensor through loss.backward(); gradients are valid finite tensors, just systematically too small by a constant factor. No assert/exception is raised — only training-curve divergence vs the ep=1 reference.

root_cause: _save_checkpoint writes the global dp_world_size into the state-dict's 'dp_world_size' field for MoE expert checkpoints. When sequence parallel is also enabled the relevant DP world size is seq_dp_world_size = dp_world_size / sp_size. On resume the checkpoint loader uses this value to re-shard expert tensors, producing the wrong split: experts get replicated/sliced across SP ranks instead of across true DP ranks, so each EP-rank loads weights for the wrong slice and starts from corrupted parameters.
invariant: After load_checkpoint, every MoE expert parameter on rank r must bit-equal the corresponding fragment that rank r wrote into the saved checkpoint.
title: MoE checkpoint records dp_world_size instead of seq_dp_world_size — wrong replication factor on resume with sequence parallel
diff_summary: Replace self.dp_world_size with self.seq_dp_world_size in the engine's MoE checkpoint metadata dict.
silent_check: Buggy code stores an integer in JSON metadata; load doesn't validate it and proceeds to slice tensors with the wrong divisor. Tensor shapes still match the partition formula so no shape assertion fires; the loaded weights are simply the wrong slice of the saved tensor.

root_cause: When the IPG bucket contains MoE params, average_tensor pre-divides each expert grad by dist.get_world_size(expert_dp_process_group)/sp_size and then skips the bucket-final divide by dist.get_world_size(dp_process_group)/sp_size. This was meant to handle the smaller EP group but it never compensates for the dp/ep ratio. The expert grad is then all-reduced over expert_dp_process_group; the final reduced value equals (sum over edp ranks)/edp_world_size — but the model's effective DP world for expert grads is dp_world_size, so the proper averaging factor should be dp_world_size, not edp_world_size. Result: expert gradients are systematically off by a factor of (dp/edp).
invariant: For matched (DP=N, EP=1) vs (DP=N, EP=2) runs with identical batch and seed, after one optimizer step the expert weights must agree to within fp32 tolerance.
title: ZeRO 1/2 expert gradients pre-divide by edp_world_size then skip the bucket-level divide — net divisor is dp/edp not dp
diff_summary: Drop the special MoE pre-divide branch; always divide the final bucket tensor by dp_world_size/sp_size at the end of average_tensor.
silent_check: Buggy code does floating-point divisions and an all-reduce — the result is a finite, valid tensor, merely scaled by the wrong constant. Optimizer step proceeds, only the loss curve diverges from the EP=1 reference.

root_cause: When drop_tokens=False, topkgating computes new_capacity via all_reduce(MAX) over expert counts, then assigns capacity=new_capacity. But it forgets to recompute `locations = torch.cumsum(mask, dim=0) - 1` after this capacity update path. The old `locations` from a stale earlier mask is used to scatter tokens into expert slots — so tokens go into the wrong dispatch positions, and the combine_weights matrix maps experts back to the wrong tokens.
invariant: After the drop_tokens branch in topkgating, locations[i,j] must equal cumsum(mask[:,j])[i] - 1 for every (i,j) where mask[i,j]==1.
title: topkgating drop_tokens=False does not recompute locations after capacity update — dispatch positions stale
diff_summary: Add `locations = torch.cumsum(mask, dim=0) - 1` immediately after `capacity = new_capacity` inside the `not drop_tokens` branch.
silent_check: Buggy code uses an integer tensor of stale offsets to index a sparse dispatch tensor — the indices are still in range, scatter succeeds, attention is computed on permuted-but-valid tokens. No exception, just wrong gradients.

root_cause: _partition_param_sec was called without the has_been_updated flag from the GatheredParameters partition path, so ds_secondary_tensor was never refreshed after the master ds_tensor changed. Similarly, checkpoint_event_epilogue did not call invalidate_secondary_tensor after _load_zero_checkpoint refilled fp16_partitioned_groups_flat (= ds_tensor). The next ZeRO++ allgather reads from the stale ds_secondary_tensor and constructs a corrupted full parameter that mixes new master weights with old secondary-partition values.
trigger_conditions: ZeRO stage 3 with hierarchical ZeRO++ (zero_quantized_weights or zero_hpz_partition_size>0)
either (a) deepspeed.zero.Init followed by GatheredParameters/_load_from_state_dict, or (b) load_checkpoint after engine init
invariant: After any update to param.ds_tensor (load_state_dict, load_checkpoint, optimizer.step), ds_secondary_tensor must equal the corresponding slice of the freshly partitioned parameter (or be marked invalid).
title: ZeRO++ ds_secondary_tensor stale after model load / checkpoint resume — dirty allgather poisons next forward
diff_summary: Pass has_been_updated to _partition_param_sec; add invalidate_secondary_tensor() at the start of checkpoint_event_epilogue.
silent_check: Both ds_tensor and ds_secondary_tensor are valid contiguous fp16/bf16 buffers; allgather succeeds and produces a full-shape parameter. Forward/backward run normally; only the loss in the first few steps is wrong (spikes/anomaly), which the user sees as a bad initialization rather than an exception.

root_cause: In quantization_utils.h::dequantize for the asymmetric path, the result line was `return conversion::to<__half>(val_deq_f);` regardless of the output template parameter T. When the kernel is instantiated with T=float, the float-typed val_deq_f gets cast to __half and back to float, throwing away ~13 bits of mantissa. The kernel still writes to the fp32 output tensor (correct shape, correct dtype), only with severely truncated precision.
trigger_conditions: dequantize template instantiated with T=float (fp32 output)
invariant: For asymmetric dequantize<float>(int8 in, scale, offset), output must equal float(in)*scale + offset to within fp32 precision (relative error <1e-6), not within fp16 precision (relative error ~1e-3).
title: Asymmetric int8 dequantize hard-codes output dtype to half — silently downcasts when caller asks for float
diff_summary: Change `conversion::to<__half>(val_deq_f)` to `conversion::to<T>(val_deq_f)` so the dequantize result keeps the requested precision.
silent_check: Buggy CUDA kernel runs to completion, writes a finite tensor of the requested fp32 dtype/shape; only the values have ~3 decimal digits of precision instead of ~7. No assert, no NaN.

root_cause: csrc/quantization/pt_binding.cpp::quantized_reduction had `const int gpu_per_node = 16;` hard-coded. The Python wrapper all_to_all_quant_reduce passes the actual local_world_size, but the C++ side ignored it. Buffer slicing inside the kernel (sz.back() / gpu_per_node, in_groups / gpu_per_node, elems_per_in_tensor / gpu_per_node) is therefore done with the wrong divisor on any non-16-GPU node — rows of the quantized intermediate get attributed to the wrong intra-node rank, producing wrong reduced gradients.
trigger_conditions: any node-local-world-size != 16 (e.g. 8 GPUs/node, single node multi-GPU, etc.)
invariant: Inside quantized_reduction, the divisor used to compute elems_per_in_tensor must equal the actual intra-node world size (devices_per_node argument), not a constant.
title: ZeRO++ all_to_all_quant_reduce hard-codes gpu_per_node=16 — wrong intra-node split on every non-16-GPU node
diff_summary: Plumb devices_per_node through quantized_reduction binding; replace all `gpu_per_node` literals with the parameter; pass local_world_size from Python.
silent_check: Buggy code performs valid CUDA kernels with valid (but wrongly-shaped) tensor views — when 8/node, divisor 16 produces a half-size buffer and reduction completes without out-of-bounds (the kernel reads/writes valid memory in the still-allocated buffer); the all_to_all uses the smaller buffer too, no shape-mismatch error. Result: gradients are silently wrong, no exception.

root_cause: load_hp_checkpoint_state used `local_rank = dist.get_local_rank()` (per-node rank 0..gpus_per_node-1) and then narrowed the loaded flat tensor at offset `local_rank * partitioned_numel`. With 2 nodes × 4 GPUs (world=8, dp=8), the local_rank wraps to 0..3 on each node, so global ranks 0 and 4 both load the SAME slice (offset 0), 1 and 5 both load slice 1, etc. Half the parameters never get the correct partition; training resumes from a hash of two unrelated weight slices.
invariant: After load_hp_checkpoint_state on rank r, checkpoint_state_partition must equal loaded_checkpoint_state.narrow(0, r * partitioned_numel, partitioned_numel) where r is the rank within self.dp_process_group.
title: Universal checkpoint stage3 multi-machine load uses local_rank instead of global DP rank for partition slicing
diff_summary: Replace local_rank = dist.get_local_rank() with rank = dist.get_rank(group=self.dp_process_group); use rank in the narrow.
silent_check: narrow(0, local_rank * size, size) is always within the padded tensor bounds, so no IndexError; the loaded partition is just the wrong slice. Loss after resume increases abnormally — user reports 'loss explodes after multi-node resume', but no exception is raised.

root_cause: In has_overflow_partitioned_grads_serial, the cross-rank `dist.all_reduce(overflow_gpu, op=MAX, group=dp_process_group)` was guarded by `if partition_gradients`. ZeRO stage 1 is partition_gradients=False, so the all-reduce was skipped. Each rank then made an independent overflow decision: ranks that saw overflow skip the step and shrink loss-scale, ranks that did not see overflow apply the step. After a few overflow events ranks have different loss_scale values and (more critically) different parameter values — DDP-equivalence is broken.
trigger_conditions: some training step where one rank's grads overflow but other ranks' do not
invariant: After has_overflow returns, every rank in dp_process_group must agree on self.overflow and self.loss_scale (and therefore on whether to take the step).
title: ZeRO-1 fp16 overflow flag broadcast only on partition_gradients path — Z1 ranks diverge on overflow
diff_summary: Remove the `if partition_gradients:` guard so dist.all_reduce(overflow_gpu, MAX) always runs, regardless of ZeRO stage.
silent_check: Buggy code skips a collective and proceeds with each rank's local overflow flag — no NCCL hang (collective is just absent, not partial), no exception. Ranks silently desync; only manifests as parameter drift over many steps.

root_cause: BF16_Optimizer.step() previously assumed param_partition.grad was already in the param's fp32 dtype because initialize_optimizer_states() did the cast at init. When grad_acc_dtype is bf16, that one-shot cast at init becomes meaningless — every subsequent step the bf16-grad accumulator gets reduced into the partition's grad slot but nothing converts it to fp32 before the wrapped Adam.step() reads it. Adam then computes m_t, v_t, and the parameter update entirely in bf16, with corresponding precision loss in the second moment.
invariant: Inside BF16_Optimizer.step(), at the moment self.optimizer.step() is called, every param_partition.grad's dtype must equal param_partition.dtype (i.e. fp32).
title: BF16_Optimizer skips fp32 cast of gradient when grad_acc_dtype != fp32 — Adam runs on bf16 grads
diff_summary: Move the per-step cast `param_partition.grad = grad_partition.to(param_partition.dtype) if dtypes differ else grad_partition` from initialize_optimizer_states() into step(); remove the now-redundant initialize_optimizer_states.
silent_check: Adam is dtype-polymorphic in PyTorch — feeding it bf16 grads with fp32 params runs without error (it casts internally per-op, losing precision in m_t/v_t). No exception; loss curve diverges slowly from the fp32-grad baseline.

root_cause: Adam_Optimizer::IncrementStep first did `_step++; if (_step != step) { recompute betta1_t/betta2_t with pow }` else `_betta1_t *= _betta1`. ZeRO-3 calls IncrementStep once per subgroup with the SAME logical `step` value. The first subgroup call increments _step to match, takes the multiplicative branch (betta_t *= betta). The second subgroup call also increments _step (now _step != step), so it falls through to the pow-recompute branch which computes pow(betta, step) — a different floating-point value than the just-multiplied one (catastrophic cancellation in pow vs repeated multiply). So subgroup 0 and subgroup 1 see different betta1_t when applying the same logical Adam step → updated weights drift apart between subgroups.
trigger_conditions: ZeRO-3 with sub_group_size > 0 OR SuperOffload (multiple subgroup optimizer calls per logical step)
invariant: Repeated calls to step_subgroup(step=k) for different subgroups must produce bit-identical bias-correction coefficients (betta1_t, betta2_t).
title: CPUAdam IncrementStep non-idempotent across same-step subgroup updates — bias-correction drifts between subgroups
diff_summary: Restructure IncrementStep into three explicit cases: step == _step (no-op early return), step == _step+1 (multiplicative update), else (pow recompute).
silent_check: Buggy CPUAdam runs to completion and updates parameters with valid finite values; the bias-correction error is on the order of float-precision differences between pow(b,k) and b*b*...*b. No assert; only manifests as cross-subgroup parameter inconsistency that grows with training.

root_cause: FP16_Optimizer.get_grad_norm computed the per-group flattened grad norm and treated all of the flat buffer as if it belonged to a non-TP parameter. So only tp_rank=0 contributed (since for non-TP params the duplicate copies on tp_rank>0 should be skipped). For genuine TP-sliced parameters this skip is wrong — the per-rank slices are different and all should sum into the global norm. Result: at TP=4 the reported total_norm is ~1/sqrt(4) = 1/2 of the true value, gradient clipping is therefore much weaker than configured.
trigger_conditions: param groups containing both TP and non-TP parameters
invariant: global_grad_norm computed by FP16_Optimizer at TP=k must equal (within fp32 tolerance) the global_grad_norm computed at TP=1 with the same global batch and seed.
title: FP16 fused optimizer grad-norm reduces only TP-rank-0 gradients — TP grad_norm undercounted by sqrt(tp_size)
diff_summary: Add _get_norm_mask_idx() to identify which slices of the flat grad belong to replicated (skip-on-non-zero-tp-rank) tensors; pass this mask to a new get_flattened_grad_norm; sum only non-masked slices.
silent_check: Wrong (smaller) total_norm is a finite scalar; gradient clipping uses a clip = max(1, norm/max_norm) so weaker clipping just means the optimizer takes a slightly larger step. No exception, only convergence drift between TP=1 and TP>1 runs.

root_cause: PipelineEngine._exec_backward_pass for non-last-stage manually calls self.optimizer.update_hp_grads(clear_lp_grads=False) because backward is invoked via torch.autograd.backward instead of optimizer.backward(). With immediate_grad_update=True the per-param backward hooks already populate fp32_groups_gradients_flat as each lp.grad is produced. The unconditional call to update_hp_grads then iterates every parameter and adds lp.grad to the fp32 accumulator a SECOND time — every gradient on PP non-last stages is doubled.
invariant: On any non-last pipeline stage, after _exec_backward_pass, fp32_groups_gradients_flat[p] must equal exactly one cast of lp.grad[p] (i.e. updated once, not twice).
title: PipelineEngine non-last-stage backward double-updates hp_grads when bfloat16_immediate_grad_update is enabled
diff_summary: Wrap the manual update_hp_grads call: `if not self._config.bfloat16_immediate_grad_update: self.optimizer.update_hp_grads(clear_lp_grads=False)`.
silent_check: Buggy code produces fp32 grads that are exactly 2x the correct value — finite, well-shaped, no NaN/Inf. The next allreduce and Adam step proceed; only the loss curve grows ~2x faster than reference and may diverge.

root_cause: set_local_grad copies the supplied tensor into the fp32 partition's grad slot but does not update self.norm_for_param_grads[param_id]. With CPU offload, scaled_global_grad_norm is later computed as the L2-aggregate of these cached per-param norms (because the actual grad lives in pinned CPU memory). The aggregate therefore reflects pre-modification gradients, while unscale_and_clip_grads applies a clip factor based on this stale norm to the modified grads — silent mis-clipping. Note that scaled_global_grad_norm also drives the loss-scale-aware clip decision in optimizer.step.
trigger_conditions: user calls safe_set_local_grad to modify a partition's gradient between backward and step (e.g. external clipping/sanitizing)
invariant: Whenever fp32 grad partition for param p is overwritten via set_local_grad, norm_for_param_grads[p] must equal _constant_buffered_norm2 of the new gradient.
title: ZeRO-3 CPU offload set_local_grad does not refresh norm_for_param_grads — gradient clipping uses pre-clipping norm
diff_summary: In _set_fp32_grad_state_partition (CPU offload branch), update self.norm_for_param_grads[param_id] = self._constant_buffered_norm2(value).
silent_check: All updates write valid finite tensors. The clipping decision is just based on a stale (typically larger) norm, so clip factor is wrong but always finite — optimizer.step proceeds, no exception.

root_cause: init_autocast_params installed lower-precision modules without instantiating a torch.amp.GradScaler. Because ZeRO stage 0 + torch.autocast doesn't go through any DeepSpeed loss-scaler path, backward propagated unscaled fp16 grads — anything below ~6e-5 magnitude flushes to 0. The optimizer step then applies near-zero updates and training stalls / converges to a degenerate solution.
trigger_conditions: no manual GradScaler in client code
invariant: When torch_autocast is enabled with dtype=fp16 and zero_optimization stage is 0, a non-trivial loss-scale must be applied before loss.backward (loss.grad_fn.scale > 1).
title: ZeRO-0 + torch.autocast(fp16) trains without a GradScaler — fp16 gradients underflow to zero
diff_summary: In DeepSpeedEngine.__init__, when (not self.zero_optimization() and torch_autocast_dtype == fp16) instantiate self.torch_autocast_z0_gradscaler = torch.amp.GradScaler; use it in backward/step/clip paths.
silent_check: Forward and backward run without exceptions; gradients are valid fp16 zeros (underflow). Optimizer.step adds ~0 to weights → loss curve flat, training silently stuck. No NaN, no overflow, no skipped step.

root_cause: In ipg_remove_grads, after triggering an async reduce_ipg_grads on bucket index k, the code immediately swaps `bucket.index = 1 - bucket.index` so the next gradient writes into bucket index (1-k). Without an explicit reduction_stream <-> current_stream wait, the backward kernel writing into bucket (1-k) on the current stream can begin before the previous reduce-scatter on bucket k has finished — and on accelerators that don't auto-resolve cross-stream data deps, both buffers (k and 1-k) are aliased through the same flat IPG tensor allocation, so the write into bucket 1-k can stomp on bucket k's still-in-flight reduce input. Loss became 0 with grad_norm 1.414 by step 3 in the user's repro.
trigger_conditions: model large enough to fill more than one ipg bucket per step
invariant: Before swapping ipg bucket index after a reduce, default stream must wait for reduction_stream to complete on accelerators where resolves_data_dependency()==False.
title: ZeRO-2 ipg double-buffer swap not synchronized — current backward writes into bucket while previous reduce still reads
diff_summary: Around the bucket.index swap, add `self.reduction_stream.wait_stream(current_stream); current_stream.wait_stream(self.reduction_stream)` guarded by `not get_accelerator().resolves_data_dependency()`.
silent_check: All operations are valid CUDA kernels writing to allocated memory; the race produces well-typed but corrupted reduced gradients. The optimizer step uses these and produces zero loss / wrong grad_norm — no exception, no CUDA error.

root_cause: In average_tensor (overlap_comm path), reduction_stream did wait_stream(current_stream) so the allreduce waits for backward to finish populating the buffer, but current_stream did NOT wait_stream(reduction_stream) afterwards. When backward of the next bucket completes faster than the previous allreduce, the next gradient gets written into the same ipg_buffer slot that allreduce is still reading, corrupting the reduce input. Equivalence (loss with vs without overlap_comm) is broken on small sequence-length / fast-compute models.
trigger_conditions: communication time per allreduce > backward compute time of next bucket
invariant: On an accelerator without automatic data-dep resolution, after triggering an async reduce on the reduction_stream, current_stream must wait for reduction_stream before reusing the IPG buffer.
title: ZeRO 1/2 reduction stream not waited by current stream — ipg_buffer rewrite races allreduce when comm > compute
diff_summary: After `stream.wait_stream(get_accelerator().current_stream())`, add `get_accelerator().current_stream().wait_stream(stream)`.
silent_check: The race produces a corrupted but valid float tensor as the allreduce input — no shape mismatch, no NCCL error. Subsequent optimizer step uses wrong gradients; loss diverges from reference but no exception is raised.

root_cause: In average_tensor's contiguous_gradients/non-extra-large branch, the code passed `self.ipg_buffer[self.ipg_index]` (the whole pre-allocated buffer of size reduce_bucket_size) to average_tensor. When the bucket flushes early (e.g. last params of a step or after a dtype switch), only elements_in_ipg_bucket are valid; the tail still holds whatever was last computed there. Those stale floats get included in the all-reduce sum and the divide-by-world-size, contaminating the per-rank averaged gradient slice for the genuine grads near the end of the buffer.
trigger_conditions: elements_in_ipg_bucket < reduce_bucket_size (i.e. bucket flushed before fill)
invariant: The tensor passed to average_tensor must be exactly self.ipg_buffer.narrow(0, 0, self.elements_in_ipg_bucket).
title: ZeRO-1/2 IPG buffer averaged over full allocated size — averages garbage from unused tail elements
diff_summary: Replace `self.ipg_buffer[self.ipg_index]` with `self.ipg_buffer[self.ipg_index].narrow(0, 0, self.elements_in_ipg_bucket)` in the average call.
silent_check: average_tensor still receives a contiguous fp16/bf16 tensor of valid shape; the all-reduce succeeds. The garbage tail values just bias gradients near bucket boundaries — finite numbers, no NaN, no shape mismatch.

root_cause: When a parameter's last partition is smaller than partition_numel, _avg_scatter_dense_grads built a padded_partition with `torch.empty(...)` and only copied the valid prefix into it. The trailing pad elements held arbitrary garbage from the GPU allocator. That whole padded tensor was then included in the reduce_scatter, so other ranks received contaminated padding bytes mixed into the next parameter's region (because reduce_scatter sums element-wise across ranks before slicing).
trigger_conditions: any param whose partition_numel > the slice numel for the last rank (requires padding)
invariant: Any padding bytes appended to a per-param grad partition before reduce-scatter must be exactly zero.
title: ZeRO-3 partition padding allocated with torch.empty — undefined values get reduced into other ranks' partitions
diff_summary: Replace `torch.empty(param.partition_numel(), ...)` with `torch.zeros(param.partition_numel(), ...)` for the padded_partition; also add the elements_in_ipg_bucket guard for the contiguous-gradients branch so it doesn't run when extra-large-tensor allreduce path is needed.
silent_check: Pre-fix code allocates uninitialized memory whose values vary run-to-run but are still finite; reduce_scatter completes normally; the wrong gradient values silently propagate to optimizer.step. No exception.

root_cause: single_all_to_all's reshape for the head-scatter path used `[seq_world_size, inp_shape[scatter_idx]] + inp_shape[scatter_idx+1:]` and then transposed (0,2). This collapses batch and sequence into a single dimension and reorders elements such that after the all_to_all+reshape back, query[b,s,h] no longer corresponds to the same logical token. Pre-attention QKV are permuted into the wrong (b,s,h) positions, attention is computed on scrambled tokens, and the model never converges.
trigger_conditions: scatter_idx >= 2 (head-scatter path used in the second alltoall)
invariant: For an identity test (round-trip _SeqAllToAll(scatter, gather) followed by _SeqAllToAll(gather, scatter)), output must equal input element-wise.
title: Sequence parallel single_all_to_all reshape collapses batch and seq dims — QKV permuted into wrong tokens
diff_summary: Refactor single_all_to_all to use explicit (bs, seq, num_head, head_dim) layout-aware reshapes/permutes that handle batch_dim_idx in {0,1} and scatter_idx <{2,>=2} correctly.
silent_check: Reshape/transpose run successfully — shapes line up so all_to_all_single completes, attention computes, loss is a finite tensor. The model's loss just refuses to drop because the relationship between tokens and their attention scores is broken; no exception.

root_cause: The manual-backward path (scale_loss → loss.backward) only applied optimizer.scale_if_loss / torch_autocast scaling, but forgot the AutoEP-specific multiplication by self._autoep_output_grad_scale that engine.backward applies. Since manual-backward is the recommended path for HF Trainer integrations, expert gradients in those setups are again undercount by ep_size relative to the engine.backward path.
trigger_conditions: user calls engine.scale_loss(loss).backward() manually instead of engine.backward(loss)
invariant: Across two AutoEP runs differing only in (engine.backward(loss)) vs (engine.scale_loss(loss).backward()), per-step expert weights must match within fp32 tolerance.
title: AutoEP manual loss.backward path skips ep_size loss scaling — parity with engine.backward broken
diff_summary: Factor _scale_loss_for_autoep helper; call it in both engine.backward and engine.scale_loss code paths.
silent_check: loss.backward() proceeds with a smaller-by-ep_size scalar; gradients are valid finite tensors. No assert; only a divergence between manual-backward and engine.backward training curves.

root_cause: save_checkpoint and load_checkpoint copied the entire NVMe swap_folder under `<save_dir>/<tag>/offloaded_tensors/` without per-rank subdir. With dp_size>1, every rank's local NVMe optimizer state (Adam exp_avg, exp_avg_sq slices) gets copied into the same destination directory; rsync/copytree overwrites file-by-file. The resulting checkpoint contains an arbitrary mix of per-rank slices. On load, every rank reads back the same files, so each rank initializes its optimizer state from another rank's slice → optimizer momenta no longer correspond to the parameters they belong to.
trigger_conditions: save_checkpoint OR load_checkpoint with multi-rank DP
invariant: After save_checkpoint, the on-disk path for NVMe-offloaded optimizer tensors must be unique per DP rank (e.g. .../offloaded_tensors/rank<r>/...).
title: ZeRO-3 NVMe optimizer offload writes all ranks' tensors to one shared dir — last writer wins, load gets wrong rank's state
diff_summary: Compute rank_dir = 'rank' + dp_index_to_str(rank); join offload_ckpt_dir with rank_dir in both save_checkpoint and load_checkpoint code paths; also gate the load_zero_checkpoint call by `not self.zero_nvme_offload_optimizer()` so NVMe path takes its own load route.
silent_check: copytree succeeds (last writer wins is a normal filesystem operation), torch.load on the wrong file returns a valid tensor of the right shape (all ranks' partitions are same shape under ZeRO-3), and optimizer.step uses these wrong moments without any exception. Loss after resume diverges silently.

root_cause: ds_adam_step / ds_adagrad_step (and the *_plus_copy variants) passed `params_c.size(0)` (the size of the FIRST dimension only) as the element count to the kernel's Step_8. For a Linear weight of shape (out, in), only `out` elements are stepped instead of `out*in`. The kernel happily walks `size(0)` floats from the data pointer (which is in-bounds) and writes back only those — the other (size(0)*(size(1)-1) ... ) elements never receive an update.
trigger_conditions: any tensor parameter with ndim >= 2 (e.g. linear weights, embedding tables)
invariant: After CPU Adam step, every element of every parameter tensor must change by exactly the Adam-prescribed update (within fp32 tolerance) — none should remain at its prior value.
title: CPU Adam/Adagrad uses params.size(0) instead of numel() — only the first row of multi-dim params gets updated
diff_summary: Replace `params_c.size(0)` with `params_c.numel()` in ds_adam_step, ds_adam_step_plus_copy, ds_adagrad_step, ds_adagrad_step_plus_copy.
silent_check: Kernel reads/writes within the first size(0) elements of valid contiguous memory — no segfault, no CUDA error. Loss curve diverges from a baseline run that uses GPU Adam, but no exception is raised.

root_cause: In DeepSpeedEngine._broadcast_model, dist.broadcast(p, ...) was invoked on the parameter Tensor itself (which has requires_grad=True). c10d::broadcast_ has no registered autograd kernel; PyTorch falls through with a warning that explicitly states 'may lead to silently incorrect behavior'. When the user later calls loss.backward(), autograd traverses the broadcast op as part of the computation graph and computes incorrect gradients (silently — no exception, just wrong numbers).
trigger_conditions: DeepSpeed engine init with ZeRO 1/2 (broadcast model path)
invariant: Tensor operations performed for cross-rank state synchronization at init must not be on autograd's recorded computation graph (must be inside torch.no_grad() or use .data).
title: ZeRO-3 init broadcast tracked through autograd — backward through synchronization op silently corrupts gradients
diff_summary: Wrap the for-loop over self.module.parameters() inside `with torch.no_grad():`.
silent_check: PyTorch emits a UserWarning but proceeds with the broadcast and adds a no-autograd-impl edge to the graph; first backward pass after init silently produces wrong gradients (the warning message itself says 'silently incorrect behavior'). No exception.

root_cause: _partition_param_sec issued an asynchronous device-to-device copy from the full param into ds_secondary_tensor (via .narrow(...).copy_()) but never recorded a stream-synchronization at the end. The next allgather of ds_secondary_tensor (launched by the prefetch coordinator) could be enqueued before the copy completed. Because both ops live on the same device but on different streams, the reader stream sees pre-copy contents — a stale fragment of the previous step's secondary tensor — and broadcasts it; the constructed full parameter is a mix of new values for the master partition and stale values for everyone else's secondary partition.
trigger_conditions: any forward/backward step that triggers 2nd-tensor allgather before the 2nd-tensor partition copy completes
invariant: After _partition_param_sec, get_accelerator().current_stream().synchronize() must complete before any consumer of param.ds_secondary_tensor (e.g. _all_gather_dtype) is enqueued.
title: ZeRO++ secondary partition copy not synchronized — prefetch all-gather reads garbage
diff_summary: Append `get_accelerator().current_stream().synchronize()` after the ds_secondary_tensor copy_; also flatten the if-else copy logic into one branch using `min(numel-start, partition_size)`.
silent_check: Both ops complete normally; just out of order. The reduced/all-gathered tensor is finite and well-shaped, only its values mix old and new state. Loss curve diverges from the reference but no exception is raised.

root_cause: DeepSpeedZeroOptimizer.allreduce_bucket and DeepSpeedZeroOptimizer_Stage3.allreduce_bucket had a default-valued kwarg `communication_data_type=torch.float16`. The caller never passed self.communication_data_type, so all reductions converted bf16 grads to fp16 before the all-reduce. fp16 has 1 bit less mantissa than bf16 and a 5-bit exponent vs bf16's 8 — values outside fp16's range (>~65k or <~6e-5) become Inf/0, the rest lose ~half their relative precision. Reduced gradients are therefore systematically degraded relative to the user-configured comm dtype.
trigger_conditions: user explicitly sets communication_data_type to bfloat16 (or relies on the engine to match it to the model dtype)
invariant: Inside allreduce_bucket, the dtype of tensor_to_allreduce must equal self.communication_data_type configured by the user (not torch.float16).
title: ZeRO-1/2/3 allreduce_bucket hard-codes communication_data_type=fp16 — bf16 grads silently downcast for reduction
diff_summary: Drop the default-fp16 kwarg from allreduce_bucket; assign communication_data_type = self.communication_data_type at the start of the method. Also stage_1_and_2 was patched to also cast the asynchronous all-reduce slices through tensor_to_reduce when comm dtype != tensor dtype.
silent_check: tensor.to(torch.float16) succeeds for finite bf16 values producing valid fp16, all-reduce completes, copy back to bf16 succeeds — only some values lose precision or saturate to Inf/0 silently. No exception, no overflow flag triggered.

root_cause: WarmupLR.__init__ stored its desired schedule but never wrote min_lr into self.optimizer.param_groups[0]['lr']. As a result, when the engine's first optimizer.step() runs (before lr_scheduler.step() which by convention is called after), the optimizer uses whatever lr the user instantiated the optimizer with — typically the peak lr — for one full step instead of the scheduler's warmup_min_lr (e.g. 0). With a typical 1e-4 peak lr and 0 warmup_min_lr, the first parameter update is therefore ~10000x larger than intended, often catastrophic for early training stability.
trigger_conditions: any DeepSpeed LRScheduler in {WarmupLR, LRRangeTest, OneCycle}
user reads lr_scheduler.get_last_lr() / param_group['lr'] before the first step()
optimizer.param_groups[0]['lr'] differs from scheduler's intended initial lr (which is min_lr / warmup_min_lr, typically 0)
invariant: After lr_scheduler construction (with last_batch_iteration == -1), every optimizer.param_groups[i]['lr'] must equal scheduler.get_lr()[i].
title: WarmupLR / LRRangeTest / OneCycle do not initialize optimizer group lr at construction — first step uses original lr
diff_summary: In WarmupLR/LRRangeTest/OneCycle/WarmupCosineLR __init__, when last_batch_iteration == -1 call update_lr(optimizer.param_groups, self.get_lr()) and store self._last_lr.
silent_check: Buggy code leaves the optimizer's lr at its construction value — a valid finite float. optimizer.step() takes a normal step using that value. No exception, just a single oversized update that the user might explain as 'first-step instability'.

expected_output.fixed: CLEAN: warmup correctly targets optimizer lr=0.005

title: WarmupLR ignores optimizer LR, always uses hardcoded 0.001

root_cause: In _setup_for_real_optimizer, padding was recorded only on `partition_id == world_size - 1` and set to 0 elsewhere. With large DP and a small param group, the alignment-induced padding (e.g. 1024 / 768 ranks ≈ 1.3 per rank, but applied as whole partitions of 348 elems) actually consumes the LAST THREE ranks — those ranks should report padding=348, 348, and 328 respectively, but recorded 0. _get_state_without_padding then trims only the last partition by its (wrong) padding, leaving the other padding ranks with junk values (uninitialized memory after the true end of the flattened parameter) that get treated as legitimate optimizer state on save / on subsequent get_lean_optimizer_state calls.
trigger_conditions: large DP world size where alignment forces padding to span more than one rank (e.g. dp=768, alignment=1536, group numel between two consecutive multiples)
invariant: For every (group i, rank r), groups_padding[i][r] must equal max(0, min(curr_partition_size, left_boundary + curr_partition_size - orig_group_numel)).
title: ZeRO-1/2 records padding only on last rank — middle ranks at large DP report padding=0 and contaminate optimizer state
diff_summary: Replace the last-rank-only padding computation with a per-rank computation based on left_boundary and orig_group_numel; move the calculation to after data_parallel_partitions is set so that left_boundary is well-defined.
silent_check: Buggy code stores padding=0 on a rank that actually has padding; subsequent get_state_without_padding skips no elements and the resulting checkpoint contains garbage in the trailing slot. Loading the checkpoint succeeds; only optimizer-state correctness is broken (wrong moments for the affected slot, manifesting as slow drift).

root_cause: TopKGate.__init__ created `self.wg = torch.nn.Linear(...).float()`, registering an fp32 weight with DeepSpeed. When the engine downcasts the model to fp16/bf16, wg.weight becomes fp16/bf16. TopKGate.forward then runs `if self.wg.weight.dtype != torch.float32: self.wg = self.wg.float()` — this creates a brand new Linear module whose weight is a fresh fp32 tensor copy and rebinds self.wg. The new wg.weight is NOT the ZeRO-tracked parameter, so its gradient is never reduced across ranks and the optimizer never updates it. The original (ZeRO-managed) wg.weight stays at its initialization value forever; only the orphan copy receives gradient updates that get thrown away at the end of each step (because the orphan is recreated every forward).
trigger_conditions: ZeRO stage 1/2/3 (which downcasts model parameters from fp32 to fp16/bf16)
invariant: TopKGate.wg.weight must be the same Python object across forward passes, AND its data_ptr must remain in DeepSpeed's tracked parameter set (no .float() reassignment in forward).
title: MoE TopKGate.wg silently rebound to a fresh fp32 Linear under ZeRO+fp16/bf16 — gate weight gradients never applied to the ZeRO-managed parameter
diff_summary: Remove the `.float()` from `self.wg = torch.nn.Linear(...).float()` constructor and the in-forward `if dtype != fp32: self.wg = self.wg.float()` block; instead compute logits via `torch.nn.functional.linear(input_fp32, weight=self.wg.weight.float(), bias=None)` so the cast is op-local and the parameter identity is preserved.
silent_check: Buggy code creates a new Linear and rebinds self.wg — Python attribute assignment, no exception. Forward returns valid logits, top-k routing is well-defined; loss is finite. Only the gate's parameter never moves from initialization, so routing decisions stay frozen at the initial random state and the model converges to a non-MoE-like local minimum (or never properly diversifies experts), but no error is raised.
