With activation checkpointing the router forward runs once normally and again under recompute (no grad), and the aux loss tracker was incremented in both passes, doubling the logged values.
trigger_conditions: activation recompute / checkpointing enabled (router runs twice per step)
invariant: Per training step, aux loss save_to_aux_losses_tracker must be called at most once per router forward where torch.is_grad_enabled() is True.
title: MoE aux loss tracker accumulates twice when activation checkpointing reruns router
diff_summary: Added 'and torch.is_grad_enabled()' to the training guards in aux_loss_load_balancing, seq_aux_loss_load_balancing, and apply_z_loss.

root_cause: In p2p_communication._communicate, when an encoder TP rank receives multiple gradients from corresponding decoder TP ranks, _handle_tensor_list reduced them via torch.stack(...).sum(dim=0). The fix is mean(dim=0): summing scaled the encoder gradient by the TP-fanout factor, silently inflating learning rate for encoder params.
trigger_conditions: encoder TP size != decoder TP size
invariant: When ETP < DTP, the gradient received at the encoder must equal the mean of the per-decoder-rank gradients, not the sum.
title: encoder->decoder PP gradients summed instead of averaged when ETP < DTP
diff_summary: Replaced .sum(dim=0, dtype=fp32) with .mean(dim=0, dtype=fp32) in _handle_tensor_list of p2p_communication._communicate.

root_cause: expert_gradient_scaling_factor was set to 1/ep_size, which only correctly normalized when DP equaled EDP (expert data parallel). When DP != EDP (e.g., TP != ETP makes EDP differ from DP), the resulting averaged-in-collective gradient was scaled by 1/(ep_size*edp_size) instead of 1/dp_size, silently changing effective learning rate for expert params.
invariant: Effective post-reduce expert gradient scale must equal 1/dp_size, regardless of EP and ETP values.
title: Distributed optimizer expert grad scaling wrong when TP != expert-TP
diff_summary: Changed expert_gradient_scaling_factor from 1.0/ep_size to edp_size/dp_size in DistributedDataParallel.

root_cause: group_limited_topk computed group_scores as scores.view(num_tokens, num_groups, -1).topk(2, dim=-1)[0].sum(dim=-1) — the k=2 was hardcoded instead of using num_groups//group_topk. This produced wrong group scores and therefore wrong group selection for token-to-expert routing in DeepSeek-style models.
invariant: group_scores must equal sum of top-(num_groups//group_topk) routing scores within each group (correctness check on the topk k value).
title: group_limited_topk used hardcoded k=2 instead of num_groups/group_topk
diff_summary: Changed .topk(2, dim=-1) to .topk(num_groups // group_topk, dim=-1) in group_limited_topk.

root_cause: Router/SharedExpert gate init logic ran config.init_method(self.weight) inside a get_data_parallel_rng_tracker fork only when perform_initialization=True; the else branch (perform_initialization=False) ALSO unconditionally re-initialized the weight on CPU outside any RNG fork. This silently re-randomized router weights even when the user expected them to be loaded later, with different values across DP ranks.
trigger_conditions: MoE TopKRouter or SharedExpertMLP gate creation
invariant: After Router.__init__ with perform_initialization=False, router.weight should not be re-randomized; if it is initialized, it must be identical across DP ranks.
title: MoE router weight initialized with DP RNG fork even when perform_initialization=False
diff_summary: Removed the get_data_parallel_rng_tracker().fork() wrapping and the unconditional else-branch reinit; now config.init_method runs deterministically on CPU only when perform_initialization=True.

root_cause: topk_softmax_with_capacity selected topk first then applied softmax: scores=topk(logits,k=1); probs=softmax(scores,dim=-1). With k=1, softmax of a length-1 vector is constant 1.0 with zero gradient w.r.t. logits, so the router weight received no learning signal at all when topk=1.
invariant: When moe_router_topk==1, the gradient of router probs w.r.t. router logits at the selected expert must be non-zero in expectation.
title: MoE topk=1 gradient is silently zero because softmax is applied post-topk on a [N,1] tensor
diff_summary: Added use_pre_softmax option; raise ValueError when topk==1 without pre-softmax, and added the use_pre_softmax branch that runs softmax over all experts before topk.

root_cause: Float16Module.cuda() converts all parameters and buffers to the working dtype. The router's expert_bias buffer was therefore demoted to bf16 each iteration; subsequent in-place updates of expert_bias accumulated in bf16, losing precision and silently distorting load-balancing-free routing decisions.
invariant: After each forward, TopKRouter.expert_bias.dtype must be torch.float32.
title: MoE expert_bias silently downcast to bf16 by Float16Module wrapper
diff_summary: Added _maintain_float32_expert_bias method that re-casts self.expert_bias.data to fp32 if it has been demoted; called at the start of TopKRouter.forward.

root_cause: MambaStack._select_layers_for_pipeline_parallel computed offset = pp_rank * (num_layers // pp_size), which assumed even partitioning. When num_layers_in_first/last_pipeline_stage was used, MambaStack disagreed with TransformerLayer.get_transformer_layer_offset about which layers belong to each PP rank, silently mismatching layer types/weights vs. checkpoints and corrupting the SSM/attention layer order.
trigger_conditions: Pipeline parallelism enabled with num_layers_in_first_pipeline_stage or num_layers_in_last_pipeline_stage set
Uneven layer distribution across PP stages
invariant: On every PP rank, MambaStack's selected layer offsets must equal those produced by get_transformer_layer_offset for the same uneven PP configuration.
title: Mamba hybrid PP layer selection ignores uneven first/last stage configuration
diff_summary: Replaced the simple num_layers // pp_size split with branching that mirrors get_transformer_layer_offset for first/last/middle stages when num_layers_in_first_pipeline_stage or num_layers_in_last_pipeline_stage is set.

root_cause: _bias_dropout_add_func downcasts residual to x.dtype (bf16) instead of upcasting x to residual.dtype (fp32)
invariant: When fp32_residual_connection=True, residual stream must stay in fp32
title: fp32 residual connection silently downcast to bf16

root_cause: switch_load_balancing_loss_func was called with self.config.moe_aux_loss_coeff directly. Aux loss is computed locally on each TP rank and gradients are then all-reduced; without dividing the coefficient by tp_size, the effective aux-loss gradient was multiplied by tp_size after the all-reduce, silently inflating load-balancing penalty.
invariant: Aux loss coefficient passed into switch_load_balancing_loss_func must equal config.moe_aux_loss_coeff / tp_world_size.
title: MoE aux loss not divided by tensor_model_parallel_size, over-scaled when TP>1
diff_summary: Computed moe_aux_loss_coeff = self.config.moe_aux_loss_coeff / get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size() and used it for both aux_loss and z_loss; logged tracker divides by adjusted coeff.

root_cause: LinearWithFrozenWeight.forward did not save/forward the allreduce_dgrad flag; backward then computed grad_input = grad_output @ weight without performing the cross-TP all-reduce that the dgrad needs. Downstream layers received TP-rank-local input gradients instead of the summed gradient, silently producing wrong weights for the upstream trainable layers.
trigger_conditions: ColumnParallelLinear/RowParallelLinear with frozen weights (requires_grad=False on weight)
invariant: After LinearWithFrozenWeight.backward in column-parallel mode, grad_input must be identical across TP ranks (post all-reduce).
title: LinearWithFrozenWeight backward skips TP all-reduce of dgrad when TP>1
diff_summary: Added allreduce_dgrad parameter to LinearWithFrozenWeight.forward; saved on ctx; backward now calls all_reduce on grad_input when ctx.allreduce_dgrad is True.

root_cause: TopKRouter.routing called self.apply_input_jitter(logits) AFTER computing logits = self.gating(input). The intent of input jitter is to perturb the router input, not the logits; jittering logits instead changes Z-loss reference and z-loss gradient direction, silently degrading load balancing.
invariant: apply_input_jitter must be called on the router input tensor before self.gating(input), not on logits after gating.
title: MoE input jitter applied AFTER gating instead of before, jittering gradients not inputs
diff_summary: Removed apply_input_jitter call after Z-loss in routing(); moved jitter application into the abstract forward path so it runs on the input before gating.

root_cause: ChainedOptimizer.load_state_dict iterated over inner optimizers and called their load_state_dict, but never rebuilt self.param_groups. Inner optimizers' load_state_dict replaces their internal param_groups dict, so the outer ChainedOptimizer kept references to the OLD param_groups. Subsequent learning-rate updates went to a detached groups list and never reached the actual optimizer state, silently freezing LR after resume.
trigger_conditions: ChainedOptimizer (e.g., MoE with separate expert/non-expert optimizers)
invariant: After ChainedOptimizer.load_state_dict, self.param_groups must be the concatenation of optimizer.param_groups for each inner optimizer (identity match).
title: ChainedOptimizer.load_state_dict leaves param_groups stale after EP>1 checkpoint resume
diff_summary: Added 'self.param_groups = []; for optimizer in self.chained_optimizers: self.param_groups += optimizer.param_groups' after the load loop in ChainedOptimizer.load_state_dict.

root_cause: BaseMoELayer used local_indices = global_indices[global_local_map] (fancy indexing). For 2-D global_indices with topk>1, advanced indexing collapses dimensions in a way that breaks the (token, expert_slot) layout, resulting in tokens being routed to the wrong experts on each EP rank. masked_select preserves the correct flat ordering.
invariant: local_indices.shape must equal global_local_map.sum() and the values must be the masked-selected entries of global_indices in row-major order.
title: MoE local_indices wrong via fancy indexing on bool mask when topk > 1
diff_summary: Replaced 'global_indices[global_local_map]' with 'global_indices.masked_select(global_local_map)' (and similarly for local_probs) in BaseMoELayer.

root_cause: ColumnParallelLinear/RowParallelLinear set explicit_expert_comm based on (config.sequence_parallel or self.expert_parallel). MoEAllGatherTokenDispatcher used the same predicate to decide whether to do the gather/scatter for expert routing. With TP>1 but SP=False (and EP=1), neither condition was True, so expert tokens were never gathered across TP ranks and each TP rank produced wrong (incomplete) MoE outputs.
invariant: When tensor_model_parallel_size > 1, MoE token gather/scatter must run regardless of sequence_parallel and expert_parallel flags.
title: MoE GroupedGEMM produces wrong outputs without sequence_parallel even when TP>1
diff_summary: Replaced 'config.sequence_parallel or self.expert_parallel' with 'config.tensor_model_parallel_size > 1 or self.expert_parallel' in ColumnParallelLinear, RowParallelLinear, and MoEAllGatherTokenDispatcher; added training-time error if MoE+TP without SP.

root_cause: MTPLossLoggingHelper.save_loss_to_tracker assigned total_loss_dict[name] = loss for each iteration regardless of whether the key already existed. Across multiple training iterations within one logging window, only the most recent iteration's MTP loss survived; the logged value was the last-step loss rather than the average over log_interval steps.
invariant: Within a single log_interval window, total_loss_dict[mtp_name] must equal the running sum of mtp_losses[i] across iterations until the window flushes.
title: MTP per-layer loss overwritten instead of accumulated when log_interval > 1
diff_summary: Replaced 'total_loss_dict[name] = loss' with 'if name in total_loss_dict: total_loss_dict[name] += loss; else: total_loss_dict[name] = loss'.

root_cause: train_step unconditionally called optim_instance._copy_main_params_to_param_buffer() whenever reuse_grad_buf_for_mxfp8_param_ag and overlap_param_gather were both set. On the first iteration the forward_pre_hook is disabled, so finish_param_sync() never zeros the grad buffer; copying main params into the shared param/grad buffer therefore left main param values inside main_grad, silently turning the next gradient accumulation into 'main_grad += new_grad' with non-zero start state.
trigger_conditions: First training iteration after init/checkpoint where forward_pre_hook is not yet registered
invariant: Before the first backward of any iteration, every weight's main_grad should be all zeros (or the residual of unfinished accumulation), never equal to the param data.
title: MXFP8 reuse_grad_buf pollutes main grads on first iter when forward_pre_hook is disabled
diff_summary: Added 'forward_pre_hook_enabled = len(model[0].remove_forward_pre_hook_handles) > 0' check; only invoke _copy_main_params_to_param_buffer when the hook is enabled.

root_cause: MultiLatentAttention computed softmax_scale as _yarn_get_mscale(rotary_scaling_factor, self.config.mscale) instead of self.config.mscale_all_dim. DeepSeek-V2 uses different values for the two; using mscale alone produced an attention softmax scaling that was wrong by an mscale_all_dim/mscale ratio, silently distorting attention probabilities every step.
invariant: MultiLatentAttention.softmax_scale must equal mscale*mscale/sqrt(q_head_dim) where mscale = _yarn_get_mscale(rotary_scaling_factor, config.mscale_all_dim).
title: MLA softmax_scale built from wrong mscale config field
diff_summary: Changed _yarn_get_mscale(self.config.rotary_scaling_factor, self.config.mscale) to _yarn_get_mscale(self.config.rotary_scaling_factor, self.config.mscale_all_dim); also changed default mscale_all_dim from 0.707 to 0.0 with new arg default.

root_cause: VocabParallelCrossEntropy.calculate_logits_max calls .float() on fp32 input which returns the same tensor; subsequent in-place subtraction corrupts activations saved for autograd backward
invariant: After .float() conversion, the result must not alias the original tensor when in-place operations follow
title: cross_entropy backward inplace corruption on fp32 logits

root_cause: get_vit_layer_with_local_spec set self_attention attn_mask_type to AttnMaskType.causal. ViTs require bidirectional attention over patch tokens, so a lower-triangular mask is applied by DotProductAttention every forward pass. The TE path was already correct (no_mask) by an earlier fix; only the local path was missed. Training proceeds normally, but every patch can only attend to earlier patches, distorting visual features.
trigger_conditions: ViT/CLIP encoder built via get_vit_layer_with_local_spec (non-TE local path)
Multimodal training (LLaVA-style) with image patch tokens
invariant: ViT SelfAttention.attn_mask_type must be AttnMaskType.no_mask in both TE and local layer specs.
title: ViT local layer spec uses AttnMaskType.causal instead of no_mask, silently turning bidirectional self-attention into causal
diff_summary: Change params={'attn_mask_type': AttnMaskType.causal} to AttnMaskType.no_mask in get_vit_layer_with_local_spec.
silent_check: DotProductAttention happily accepts a causal mask on a square ViT input; no exception is raised, training and validation losses look plausible, but the visual encoder learns from a wrongly masked attention pattern.

root_cause: In the cached-mask branch, GPTDataset assigned loss_mask = self.cached_loss_mask, returning the cached tensor by reference instead of a clone. Downstream code in the same __getitem__ path applies in-place modifications (e.g. zeroing the loss for pad tokens). The first sample with padding silently mutates the shared cache, so every subsequent sample served from the cache starts from a polluted mask.
trigger_conditions: create_attention_mask=False so the cached-mask branch is taken
Sequences with padding so loss_mask is mutated per-sample by mask_loss_or_position fill
invariant: GPTDataset.cached_loss_mask must equal a tensor of all-ones at the start of every __getitem__ call.
title: GPTDataset returns aliased cached_loss_mask, downstream in-place padding mutates the shared cache and corrupts later samples
diff_summary: Replace loss_mask = self.cached_loss_mask with loss_mask = self.cached_loss_mask.clone().
silent_check: Returning a tensor view rather than a clone is legal Python; no exception is raised, loss values stay finite, but loss_mask of later batches has growing zeros and the per-token loss is silently under-counted.

root_cause: GradReducePipeline.gradient_reduce_preprocessing was passed gbuf.data (the entire buffer) instead of bucket.data (the per-bucket slice). gradient_scaling preprocessing therefore divided every byte of the joint gradient buffer once per bucket, yielding cumulative scaling factor of (1/dp_size)**num_buckets on the affected ranges instead of (1/dp_size). All-reduce/reduce-scatter then communicated wrongly scaled gradients with no shape mismatch.
invariant: After gradient_reduce_preprocessing, the magnitude of bucket.data must equal the pre-scaled magnitude divided by gradient_scaling_factor (not by gradient_scaling_factor**num_buckets).
title: Megatron-FSDP GradReducePipeline scales gbuf.data instead of bucket.data, applying gradient scaling to the wrong tensor span
diff_summary: Change gradient_reduce_preprocessing(gbuf.data, ...) to gradient_reduce_preprocessing(bucket.data, ...).
silent_check: Both gbuf.data and bucket.data are valid contiguous tensors; division does not raise; gradients are smaller but finite, optimizer steps complete, and only the loss curve eventually deviates from the correctly-scaled run.

root_cause: DistributedDataParallel computed target_gradient_scaling_factor = 1.0 / parallel_state.get_data_parallel_world_size() without with_context_parallel=True. With CP enabled the gradient reduction collective spans the dp*cp ranks, so the gradients should be divided by dp_size*cp_size. Only dividing by dp_size leaves a residual factor of cp_size in the parameter updates.
invariant: When context_parallel_size > 1, the gradient_scaling_factor used by DDP must be 1 / (data_parallel_world_size * context_parallel_size).
title: DistributedDataParallel target_gradient_scaling_factor uses get_data_parallel_world_size without context_parallel, so gradients are over-scaled by cp_size when CP is enabled
diff_summary: Add with_context_parallel=True to the get_data_parallel_world_size() calls used to compute target_gradient_scaling_factor and the DDP gradient_scaling_factor.
silent_check: World-size queries return positive ints; division never errors; gradients flow normally and the optimizer steps; only after many steps does the cp_size-scale-off learning rate manifest as slower convergence relative to a CP=1 baseline.

root_cause: forward_step_calc_loss set MTPLossAutoScaler.set_loss_scale(loss_scale / num_microbatches) but DSAIndexerLossAutoScaler was never given a per-microbatch divisor. As a result the DSA indexer auxiliary loss accumulates num_microbatches times into the gradient instead of being averaged, contributing a (num_microbatches)x larger gradient than the main loss.
invariant: DSAIndexerLossAutoScaler.loss_scale at backward time must equal loss_scale / num_microbatches when calculate_per_token_loss=False.
title: DSA indexer loss is not divided by num_microbatches in forward_step_calc_loss, so the auxiliary loss gradient is overweighted by a factor of num_microbatches
diff_summary: Add a parallel DSAIndexerLossAutoScaler.set_loss_scale(loss_scale / num_microbatches) block alongside the existing MTPLossAutoScaler block in forward_step_calc_loss.
silent_check: DSAIndexerLossAutoScaler is just a multiplicative wrapper; backward proceeds normally and produces no exception, optimizer steps as usual, but the DSA branch dominates the gradient signal in proportion to num_microbatches.

root_cause: _make_fused_ops creates new GroupedLinear instances for the fused FC1/activation/FC2 path. backward_dw was called on the new instances, but DDP had registered the wgrad-accumulate-and-reduce hooks on the ORIGINAL self.linear_fc1/fc2 modules. Hooks therefore never fired, param.grad was not cleared, and AccumulateGrad performed an additional in-place add into main_grad on the next iteration, silently double-counting expert weight gradients.
trigger_conditions: TE GroupedLinear with fused operations (TEGroupedMLP fused path)
invariant: After every TEGroupedMLP.backward_dw call, _trigger_wgrad_accumulation_and_reduce_hooks must be invoked exactly once on linear_fc1 and once on linear_fc2.
title: TEGroupedMLP fused-ops backward_dw skips _trigger_wgrad_accumulation_and_reduce_hooks on the original linear modules, so DDP never zeros param.grad and AccumulateGrad double-counts
diff_summary: After fused_children backward_dw calls, add explicit self.linear_fc2._trigger_wgrad_accumulation_and_reduce_hooks() and self.linear_fc1._trigger_wgrad_accumulation_and_reduce_hooks().
silent_check: The new GroupedLinear instances do produce wgrads that flow into main_grad; nothing raises; the only effect is that main_grad accumulates one extra copy per step, slowly inflating the effective learning rate for expert weights.

root_cause: forward_backward_pipelining_with_interleaving issued an isend to the next stage and immediately called deallocate_output_tensor without waiting on send_next_wait_handle. Because isend's HtoD copy is asynchronous, the destination buffer on the next rank could end up with whatever value happened to be left in memory by the time the deallocation reuse cycle began. Training continued with subtly corrupted forward activations propagated down the pipeline.
invariant: Whenever deallocate_pipeline_outputs=True, every send_next isend handle must have wait() called before deallocate_output_tensor on the same output_tensor.
title: Interleaved 1F1B forgets to wait on async P2P send before deallocating the source buffer, sending corrupted activations to the next pipeline stage
diff_summary: Insert send_next_wait_handle.wait() and reset to None right before deallocate_output_tensor in both branches of the interleaved loop.
silent_check: isend returns a future that, when not waited on, simply does not raise; deallocate_output_tensor frees storage that may have been already copied or may be partially copied; the next stage receives a tensor of the correct shape and dtype but with random contents from a recycled buffer, training proceeds without exception.

root_cause: prepare_input_tensors_for_wgrad_compute only called grad_output.contiguous() and assumed all_gathered_input was already contiguous. Some upstream paths (NeMo SFT QAT inputs, some reshape/transpose chains) hand in a strided tensor, but fused_weight_gradient_mlp_cuda.wgrad_gemm_accum_* indexes the buffer via flat data_ptr arithmetic. The kernel reads the wrong elements yet the tensor metadata looks valid, so the wgrad accumulation produces silently incorrect numbers.
trigger_conditions: Sequence parallel + TP > 1 with non-contiguous gathered activations (e.g. NeMo SFT QAT codepath)
invariant: all_gathered_input.is_contiguous() must be True at the entry of prepare_input_tensors_for_wgrad_compute.
title: prepare_input_tensors_for_wgrad_compute does not enforce all_gathered_input.contiguous(), so wgrad GEMM reads a non-contiguous strided tensor as if it were contiguous
diff_summary: Add all_gathered_input = all_gathered_input.contiguous() right after grad_output.contiguous().
silent_check: Calling a CUDA kernel with a non-contiguous input does not raise from CUDA; the kernel reads garbage strides but completes; wgrad values are arbitrarily wrong but finite, and training proceeds normally.

title: MoE aux loss not scaled by num_tokens in per_token_loss mode

root_cause: tensor_parallel.checkpoint always dispatched to CheckpointFunction.apply, even during graph warmup or capture. CheckpointFunction tries to recompute the saved forward inside the graph context, which corrupts the captured graph because random states and saved tensors get rewritten between warmup and capture passes. The result is a captured graph that on replay produces values that do not match the eager reference.
trigger_conditions: CUDA graph capture for the same module (cuda_graph_modules)
invariant: When is_graph_warmup() or is_graph_capturing() is True, tensor_parallel.checkpoint must invoke function(*args) directly without entering CheckpointFunction.apply.
title: tensor_parallel.checkpoint runs CheckpointFunction during CUDA graph warmup, causing graph capture to record stale recomputed activations
diff_summary: At the top of checkpoint(), short-circuit to function(*args) when is_graph_warmup() or is_graph_capturing() is True.
silent_check: CheckpointFunction.apply during warmup does not raise; the captured graph replays without error and the activations look numerically reasonable, but they no longer match the eager-mode reference and the loss curve drifts away from runs without CUDA graphs.

root_cause: When the user_input tensor is the SAME storage as cudagraph_input (data_ptr equality), copy_ amounts to a self-copy that semantically still launches a kernel. In specific reuse patterns the source and destination data pointers were intentionally identical so no copy was needed, but cudagraph_input.copy_(user_input) was always issued and could overwrite a value that another op had just written, especially under certain stream orderings.
trigger_conditions: CUDA graphs enabled with input/output buffer reuse across runners
Sequence of layers where the previous layer's output is the next layer's input alias
invariant: cudagraph_input.copy_(user_input) must only be issued when user_input.data_ptr() != cudagraph_input.data_ptr().
title: _CudagraphReplayNode unconditionally copies user_input into cudagraph_input even when the data pointers already match, overwriting in-place results from preceding ops
diff_summary: Guard the cudagraph_input.copy_(user_input) call with if user_input.data_ptr() != cudagraph_input.data_ptr().
silent_check: Self-copies via copy_ never raise; subsequent reads succeed; the only effect is that values produced concurrently on adjacent streams may be silently overwritten with stale data, leading to numerical drift across replays.

root_cause: _ParamAndGradBucketGroup created a CudaGraphManager for copy_params_from_grad_buffer without num_warmup_steps=0, so the cast graph was warmed up before capture. Combined with cuda_graph_use_single_mempool=True and lack of per-VPP stage scoping, multiple VPP stages shared mempool and warmup buffers, so the captured cast graph for one VPP stage could write into another stage's parameter buffer.
trigger_conditions: DDP enable_cuda_graph=True with virtual pipeline parallel (interleaved schedule)
Multiple VPP stages on the same device
invariant: DDP cast cudagraphs must be created with num_warmup_steps=0 and tagged with the current vp_stage so that VPP stages do not share captured buffer pools.
title: DDP cast cudagraph manager runs warmup steps and shares mempool across virtual pipeline stages, corrupting captured param-cast outputs across VPP
diff_summary: Pass num_warmup_steps=0 to the DDP CudaGraphManager('copy_params_from_grad_buffer') and set cuda_graphs.Cudagraph_VPP_Stage = self.vp_stage before each MambaStack/TransformerBlock forward.
silent_check: Warmup of the cast graph is just an extra forward pass; capture proceeds; replay returns parameters of correct shape and dtype, but values may have been overwritten by the warmup or by a sibling VPP stage, so optimizer updates are applied to silently corrupted cast weights.

root_cause: _build_model_and_main_param_groups built shard_model_param as model_param.view(-1)[range] without .detach(). Unlike the FP16/BF16 branch (which goes through main_param.detach() copies), the FP32 view kept grad_fn alive. As soon as anything autograd-eligible touched the shard, an extra grad chain was created, leading to silently doubled gradient contributions for FP32 parameters and inconsistent state with the FP16/BF16 path.
trigger_conditions: DistributedOptimizer enabled with FP32 master parameters
Mixed precision training where some params remain FP32 (e.g. embeddings, layernorm)
invariant: Every shard_model_param entry created in _build_model_and_main_param_groups must satisfy shard_model_param.requires_grad == False and shard_model_param.grad_fn is None.
title: DistributedOptimizer FP32 shard_model_param uses non-detached view, so the parameter shard participates in autograd and accumulates spurious grad_fn
diff_summary: Change shard_model_param = model_param.view(-1)[start:end] to shard_model_param = model_param.detach().view(-1)[start:end].
silent_check: Creating a non-detached view never raises; autograd eagerly hooks into the shard but does not error on the first backward; the accumulated effect is that FP32 parameters receive a duplicated or otherwise inconsistent gradient compared to the BF16/FP16 path.

root_cause: _ParamAndGradBucket initialized param_to_index by walking params and assigning offset += param.numel(), but the global param_index_map already had per-param padded offsets. The two layouts diverged whenever a param's size was not a multiple of dp_world_size. param_to_index was then used by the distributed optimizer to slice param_data, so the optimizer wrote/read different slices than where the gradients lived.
trigger_conditions: Bucket with multiple params where at least one param.numel() is not a multiple of data_parallel_world_size
Adjacent params therefore receive runtime padding between them
invariant: For every param in bucket, bucket.param_to_index[param] must equal (param_index_map[param][0] - bucket.offset, param_index_map[param][1] - bucket.offset).
title: _ParamAndGradBucket builds local param_to_index from naive concatenation, ignoring per-param padding so optimizer reads from misaligned offsets when distributed optimizer pads to data_parallel_world_size
diff_summary: Replace local-offset accumulation in _ParamAndGradBucket with derivation from param_index_map: param_to_index[param] = (global_start - offset, global_end - offset).
silent_check: Both index ranges have the right total numel; tensor slices succeed; only the values landing at each location are wrong, so the optimizer updates the wrong slice of weights and gradients without raising any error.

root_cause: MoELayer.backward_dw only invoked self.experts.backward_dw() and (when shared_experts requested) self.shared_experts.backward_dw(). The new latent projection layers fc1_latent_proj/fc2_latent_proj were never asked to compute their weight gradients, so their main_grad stayed at zero across every microbatch. The optimizer happily applied (lr * 0) to those parameters every step, freezing them at their initialization.
trigger_conditions: MoE layer with config.moe_latent_size set (latent MoE / DeepSeek-style projection)
