root_cause: On epoch rollover Trainer reset epoch counters and called dataset.reshuffle(), but never reset dataset.start_index. The IterableDataset therefore skipped the first global_train_examples_seen_this_epoch instances of the new epoch, silently dropping them from training.
trigger_conditions: training spans more than one epoch (max_epochs > 1)
invariant: at the start of every epoch, self.dataset.start_index must equal 0
title: Multi-epoch training does not reset dataset.start_index, so the next epoch resumes from the previous epoch's offset
diff_summary: added self.dataset.start_index = 0 to the post-epoch reset block, alongside global_train_examples_seen_this_epoch = 0 and the reshuffle call

root_cause: IterableDataset was constructed with seed=seed+(train_config.epoch or 0) and reshuffle() did self.seed += 1. After a restart at epoch=N the dataset received seed+N as base and then was incremented again, producing a different shuffle order than the original run had used at the same epoch. This silently changed the data ordering across resumes.
trigger_conditions: training resumes from a checkpoint that is past the first epoch
invariant: the global indices produced by IterableDataset for (seed, epoch) must be identical across a fresh run and a resumed run
title: Restart in later epochs uses seed+epoch as PRNG seed, mixing epoch into seed irreversibly and corrupting reshuffle
diff_summary: split seed and epoch into separate fields, used PCG64(seed=seed+epoch) inside _build_global_indices, and changed reshuffle to take an explicit epoch arg rather than mutating self.seed

root_cause: per_param_min/max/sum/norm tensors were appended without explicit device, defaulting to CPU. The subsequent dist.all_reduce was then performed on CPU tensors while NCCL only supports GPU tensors; this either silently used the gloo backend (different reduction semantics, slower) or returned partially-reduced values when ranks ended up on different devices. Fix forces all metric tensors to the GPU device.
invariant: every tensor passed to dist.all_reduce/dist.reduce in clip_grads_and_collect_metrics must reside on the CUDA device, not CPU
title: Optimizer metric tensors are kept on CPU, causing per-rank cross-device mismatch on the all_reduce path
diff_summary: appended .to(device=device, dtype=torch.float32) (and dtype/device kwargs to torch.linalg.vector_norm) to all per_param metric tensors before they are concatenated and reduced

root_cause: z_squared / mask.mean() instead of (z_squared * mask).mean() — wrong reduction
invariant: z_loss with mean reduction should be a scalar; buggy version returns unreduced tensor
title: z_loss mean reduction divides by mask fraction instead of masked mean

root_cause: In Trainer the cross-entropy and z-loss were reduced across all ranks before logging, but lb_batch_loss (MoE load-balancing loss) and moe_z_batch_loss were missed. Each rank logged its local value, so the wandb metric reflected only rank 0's mini-batch instead of the global mean, giving misleading load-balance behavior and misreporting MoE training health.
invariant: after the metric reduction block, lb_batch_loss and moe_z_batch_loss must be identical on every rank (mean across ranks)
title: MoE load-balance and z-loss aux losses logged without all-reduce, so each rank reports its local value
diff_summary: added two if blocks that call dist.reduce(loss, 0) and div_(get_world_size()) for lb_batch_loss and moe_z_batch_loss when not None

root_cause: Optimizer.clip_grads_and_collect_metrics divided by a hardcoded num_model_replicas=1 even when HSDP was using multiple replicas. Each replica contributed identical gradient norms; without dividing by the replica count, all_reduce sums them and the reported norm is N times the true value, leading to spurious clipping decisions and wrong logged grad_norm.
invariant: with N model replicas in HSDP, all_reduced grad_norm metric must be divided by N before being reported
title: Optimizer collects metrics with num_model_replicas == 1 hardcoded, so HSDP norms are N times too large
diff_summary: moved the num_model_replicas determination into clip_grads_and_collect_metrics (passed via train.py) and applied / self.num_model_replicas to the all_reduced sums and norms

root_cause: After the dist.all_reduce(SUM) in HYBRID_SHARD, identical replica contributions are summed N times. The original code consumed those sums directly, so per-param avg metrics and grad_norm metrics ended up N times larger than the true value. Fix divides the all-reduced tensor (all_sums_norms_numels and all_norms) by self.num_model_replicas before splitting and using.
invariant: for HSDP with N replicas, sum_after_all_reduce / N must equal the true global sum; per_param_avg_metrics computed from this should match a reference single-replica run
title: Reduced sums/norms not divided by num_model_replicas in HSDP, optimizer metrics inflated by replica count
diff_summary: added all_sums_norms_numels = all_sums_norms_numels / self.num_model_replicas (and all_norms /= num_model_replicas in the no-collect branch) right after the all_reduce sum

root_cause: _make_state_dict_compatible returned a remapped state_dict but FullCheckpointer threw away the og_keys_to_new mapping when calling load_fsdp_optim_state. The optimizer state was then loaded against the new model keys without translation, so optimizer state for many params was either silently zeroed or attached to the wrong tensor.
trigger_conditions: training resumes with a different block_group_size than at save time
invariant: after FullCheckpointer.restore_checkpoint with load_optimizer_state=True, optimizer.state must contain entries for every parameter in fsdp_model.parameters() and the values must match the saved checkpoint
title: FullCheckpointer rebuilds optim state with old parameter keys, dropping state for renamed params after block_group_size change
diff_summary: captured (state_dict_to_load, og_keys_to_new) from _make_state_dict_compatible and added _make_optim_state_dict_compatible(optim_state_dict, og_keys_to_new) before load_fsdp_optim_state

root_cause: get_param_groups identified norm parameters via the substring '.norm.' which only matches when there is a child name after .norm. For QK layer norms (q_norm.weight, k_norm.weight) the FQN ends with '.q_norm.weight' so the dot after norm never appears and the weight is silently routed to the decay group, applying weight_decay to a normalization layer's gain.
trigger_conditions: model has LayerNorm/RMSNorm modules whose param fully-qualified name does not have anything after .norm (e.g. blocks.0.attn.q_norm.weight)
invariant: all parameters whose name contains '.norm' (with or without a child) must end up in the no_decay group when no_decay_norm_and_bias is true
title: param-group classifier uses '.norm.' regex requiring trailing dot, treating q_norm/k_norm/ff_norm leaf weights as decay params
diff_summary: changed the substring check from '.norm.' to '.norm' so it matches both nested and leaf norm parameters

root_cause: all_sums.unsqueeze(-1), all_norms.unsqueeze(-1), all_numels.unsqueeze(-1) were concatenated on dim=-1 and then reduced. After dist.reduce, all_sums_norms_numels.split(1) split per-parameter rows instead of separating the three categories, so the per-param avg metrics became a meaningless mix of sums/norms/numels.
trigger_conditions: collect_param_metrics path that combines sums, norms, and numels into one all-reduce
invariant: after dist.reduce and split(1), the three pieces all_sums/all_norms/all_numels must each have shape (num_params,)
title: all_sums_norms_numels concatenated along last dim and reduced wrongly, mixing sums/norms/numels into one slot
diff_summary: changed unsqueeze(-1)/dim=-1 to unsqueeze(0)/dim=0 so the concat stacks along a new leading dimension and split(1) cleanly returns the three category tensors

root_cause: Before this commit MemMapDataset was constructed without passing a memmap_dtype, defaulting to uint16. When the actual on-disk file was uint32 (because vocab_size > 2^16), reading two-byte chunks silently produced wrong token ids without any type error. Fix exposes effective_memmap_dtype on DataConfig and threads it through build_memmap_dataset.
trigger_conditions: MemMap dataset built from train_config without an explicit dtype
invariant: MemMapDataset(memmap_dtype) must equal np.uint32 (or wider) when train_config.model.vocab_size > 2**16
title: DataConfig defaults memmap_dtype to uint16 silently, so vocab_size > 2^16 truncates token ids on load
diff_summary: added DataConfig.memmap_dtype field and effective_memmap_dtype property; passed train_config.data.effective_memmap_dtype into MemMapDataset() in build_memmap_dataset

root_cause: The clipping helpers were called with collect_param_metrics=True every step, regardless of the outer collect_param_metrics flag. This silently bypassed the metrics_log_interval gate (forcing host-device sync to compute clipping_rate every step) and produced metric values that did not match the requested logging cadence.
invariant: when collect_param_metrics is False at the outer call, _do_adaptive_clipping/_do_global_fixed_clipping must also be invoked with collect_param_metrics=False and clipping_rate must not be added to all_metrics
title: _do_adaptive_clipping/_do_global_fixed_clipping hardcode collect_param_metrics=True, forcing per-step host-device sync and ignoring metrics_log_interval
diff_summary: passed the outer collect_param_metrics through to _do_adaptive_clipping and _do_global_fixed_clipping, and gated the clipping_rate metric assignment on collect_param_metrics

root_cause: pos_sin/pos_cos cached in float32, not cast to match q_ dtype (bf16/fp16)
invariant: In apply_rotary_pos_emb, pos_sin.dtype and pos_cos.dtype must match t.dtype
title: RoPE sin/cos missing type_as — dtype mismatch in mixed precision

root_cause: Every Mitchell-init code path (OLMoBlock, OLMoSequentialBlock, OLMoLlamaBlock, and OLMo wte init) literally assigned cutoff_factor = 3.0, completely ignoring config.init_cutoff_factor. User configs that set a different cutoff (e.g. 4 or 6) silently produced narrower truncated-normal weight distributions than requested.
invariant: for init_fn=mitchell, the cutoff_factor used by init_normal must equal config.init_cutoff_factor (falling back to 3.0 only when None)
title: Mitchell init hardcodes cutoff_factor=3.0, ignoring user-supplied init_cutoff_factor across blocks and embeddings
diff_summary: replaced hardcoded `cutoff_factor = 3.0` with `cutoff_factor = self.config.init_cutoff_factor or 3.0` in the three OLMo block variants and in OLMo.reset_parameters' wte init path

root_cause: The final linear decay segment is meant to take over after a cosine schedule has already decayed the LR to alpha_f * base_lr. The buggy version constructed `LinearLR(start_factor=1.0, end_factor=alpha_f)` which jumps the LR back up to the base learning rate at the handoff, and then decays only to alpha_f over the tail. The correct settings continue from `alpha_f` down to `alpha_f**2`. Result is a silent LR spike + wrong final LR.
trigger_conditions: scheduler concatenates cosine-with-warmup followed by linear final decay
Training enters the post-cosine linear segment (global_step > t_max)
invariant: scheduler.get_last_lr() must be continuous across the cosine-to-linear handoff at step=t_max
title: Final linear-decay scheduler uses wrong start/end factors (decays from 1.0 to alpha_f instead of alpha_f to alpha_f^2)
diff_summary: Set start_factor=alpha_f and end_factor=alpha_f**2 for the final LinearLR
silent_check: LinearLR accepts the wrong factors without complaint; LR values change but stay finite, so optimizer.step proceeds and training continues with a silently corrupted schedule.

root_cause: init_std used directly instead of init_std * sqrt(d_model) for embeddings
invariant: embedding weight std should be init_std * sqrt(d_model)
title: Embedding init std missing sqrt(d_model) factor — embeddings 16x too small

root_cause: When distributing the leftover (unaligned) indices across workers, the buggy code did `left_overs = indices[truncated_size + worker_info.id : truncated_size + worker_info.id + worker_info.num_workers]`, which gives each worker a contiguous slice of `num_workers` indices starting at its id (so workers overlap and miss other leftovers). The fix uses strided slicing `indices[truncated_size + worker_info.id :: worker_info.num_workers]` so each worker independently picks its share.
trigger_conditions: Total indices not divisible by device_batch_size
invariant: Union of leftover indices across all workers must equal the full set of leftover indices, with no overlap
title: IterableDataset leftover indices distributed wrongly across workers
diff_summary: Replace contiguous slice with strided slicing for leftover-index assignment per worker
silent_check: Slicing always returns a (possibly empty) array; downstream collator processes whatever indices it gets without raising, so training continues with silently duplicated/missing samples.

root_cause: On epoch rollover the trainer set `self.epoch = epoch + 1` and reset `global_train_examples_seen_this_epoch = 0`, called `dataset.reshuffle()`, but forgot to reset `self.dataset.start_index = 0`. The IterableDataset therefore continued slicing the new (reshuffled) global indices starting from the previous epoch's offset, dropping that prefix of the new epoch and shortening it by the same amount.
invariant: At the start of every epoch the dataset must yield exactly len(dataset) examples in that epoch
title: Dataset start_index not reset when starting a new epoch
diff_summary: Add `self.dataset.start_index = 0` before reshuffle on epoch transition
silent_check: Slicing past the start of an array is just an empty/short slice—no exception. Training continues with a silently truncated epoch.

root_cause: OLMoSequentialBlock.reset_parameters unconditionally called `init_normal(self.ff_proj, std, cutoff_factor, ...)`. When `use_mup=True`, ff_proj is a `MuReadout` module whose readout weights must remain at the muP zero/special initialization; the unconditional re-init overwrites that with a regular truncated-normal, silently breaking the muP coordinate-check guarantee that activation magnitudes are width-independent.
trigger_conditions: use_mup enabled OR full_megatron init_fn (where ff_proj should keep MuReadout's zero init)
invariant: If use_mup=True, ff_proj.weight at end of init must remain at MuReadout's zero/scaled init (not truncated-normal with std=init_std)
title: Block readout init unconditionally re-initializes ff_proj, overwriting muP zero-init
diff_summary: Wrap the readout `init_normal` call in `if not self.config.use_mup`
silent_check: init_normal accepts any nn.Linear/MuReadout-shaped weight and just rewrites the data tensor in place; no exception is raised, the model trains, only its initialization is silently wrong.

root_cause: When constructing QK normalization layers, `k_norm` correctly used `elementwise_affine=config.attention_layer_norm_with_affine` but `q_norm` was hard-coded to `elementwise_affine=True`. With `attention_layer_norm_with_affine=False` the model silently normalizes q with learnable scale/bias but k without, breaking symmetry between q and k and adding parameters that the user did not request.
invariant: q_norm.weight.requires_grad == k_norm.weight.requires_grad; both must follow attention_layer_norm_with_affine
title: q_norm forced to elementwise_affine=True regardless of attention_layer_norm_with_affine
diff_summary: Pass `elementwise_affine=config.attention_layer_norm_with_affine` to both q_norm and k_norm builds
silent_check: Both LayerNorm flavours are valid; constructor succeeds, forward and backward run normally, only parameter counts and gradients differ silently.

root_cause: wte was constructed with `nn.Embedding(config.vocab_size, ...)` but the output projection `ff_out` was sized for `config.embedding_size or config.vocab_size`. When embedding_size > vocab_size, ff_out has more output classes than the embedding table has rows, so the extra logits backprop into nothing on the embedding side and the loss is computed over rows that have no corresponding learnable embedding. Logits for ids in [vocab_size, embedding_size) silently bias the softmax denominator.
trigger_conditions: embedding_size set distinct from vocab_size (e.g. embedding_size=50304, vocab_size=50257—padded for hardware alignment)
invariant: wte.num_embeddings must equal ff_out.out_features (= embedding_size or vocab_size)
title: Token embedding sized by vocab_size instead of embedding_size, mismatching ff_out width
diff_summary: Construct wte with `embedding_size or vocab_size` rows
silent_check: All token ids in input data lie in [0, vocab_size) so no embedding lookup is out of range; the size mismatch only matters in the loss/softmax, which still produces a finite loss.

root_cause: flash_attn expects (B,S,H,D) but receives (B,H,S,D) without transpose
invariant: flash_attn input dim1 must be seq_len, not num_heads
title: Flash attention input layout wrong — head and sequence dims swapped

root_cause: Starting in torch 2.1, FSDP no longer triggers the user's reset_parameters() automatically when materializing meta-device parameters. The buggy script created the OLMo model with init_device='meta', wrapped with FSDP, and never explicitly called `olmo_model.reset_parameters()` afterwards. Parameters are therefore left with whatever default contents FSDP produces (effectively uninitialized/zero-filled), silently destroying the carefully designed init scheme.
invariant: After FSDP wrap, summary stats of every parameter must match the init_fn's expected mean/std
title: Missing reset_parameters() after FSDP wrap on torch>=2.1 leaves model with default-initialized weights
diff_summary: Call `olmo_model.reset_parameters()` immediately after FSDP wrap
silent_check: FSDP successfully materializes the meta tensors with default contents; no exception. The model trains, but starts from a near-zero init that drastically changes loss dynamics.

root_cause: When building the readout `ff_out`, every other Linear in the model passed `device=config.init_device` so it could be created on the meta device and later materialized by FSDP with the configured init. The buggy version omitted this kwarg for `ff_out`, so it was always built on the default device with default kaiming init, escaping the init pipeline. The readout therefore carries the wrong init scale and lives on the wrong device until FSDP later moves it.
invariant: After model construction, every learnable parameter's device must equal config.init_device
title: ff_out nn.Linear constructed without device=init_device, breaking meta-init flow
diff_summary: Add `device=config.init_device` to ff_out's nn.Linear
silent_check: nn.Linear without device kwarg succeeds and uses CPU default init; nothing raises and FSDP later places the param on GPU—the only effect is silently using a different init distribution.

root_cause: `reset_parameters()` was nested inside `if infshapes is not None:` together with `apply_infshapes`. For the standard-parametrization baseline (`infshapes=None`) the code therefore skipped reset_parameters entirely, leaving FSDP-materialized parameters with their default (often near-zero) values. Comparison curves and any downstream training look completely off without raising an error.
trigger_conditions: mup_olmo coord-check load_model path used for SP (standard-param) baseline
infshapes argument is None (i.e. running the SP comparison rather than a muP run)
invariant: olmo_model.reset_parameters() must be called whenever the model is freshly built, regardless of mup mode
title: load_model in mup coord-check skips reset_parameters when infshapes is None
diff_summary: Dedent `olmo_model.reset_parameters()` so it runs unconditionally
silent_check: Skipping a method call never raises; FSDP-wrapped model uses default init silently and produces finite (but wrong) outputs.

root_cause: DeepSpeedTrainer built its DeepSpeed config with `"scheduler": {"type": "WarmupLR", ...}`. WarmupLR only ramps up to the max LR and then holds it constant—it never decays. The intended schedule was WarmupDecayLR which ramps then linearly decays. Buggy training therefore runs at peak LR for the entire post-warmup duration, silently overshooting the planned schedule.
trigger_conditions: DeepSpeedTrainer in use (configs ending in -lumi-deepspeed.yaml etc.)
Long enough training that decay matters
invariant: After warmup, learning rate must be monotonically decreasing toward warmup_min_lr; not constant
title: DeepSpeed scheduler set to WarmupLR instead of WarmupDecayLR (no decay phase)
diff_summary: Set scheduler type to WarmupDecayLR for the DeepSpeed config
silent_check: Both WarmupLR and WarmupDecayLR are valid DeepSpeed scheduler types; engine accepts the config and steps; LR just plateaus instead of decaying.

root_cause: DeepSpeedTrainer hard-coded `warmup_min_lr=0.0` and omitted `warmup_type='linear'`. Combined, the warmup ramp starts from exactly 0 (rather than 10% of base lr) and uses DeepSpeed's default warmup interpolation, producing a different shape than the OLMo trainer for the equivalent config. Training runs to completion but with a silently mismatched warmup schedule.
invariant: DeepSpeed warmup LR profile must match the OLMo trainer's warmup profile for an equivalent configuration
title: DeepSpeed warmup_min_lr=0 instead of base_lr*0.1, also missing warmup_type=linear
diff_summary: Set warmup_min_lr=lr*0.1 and add warmup_type=linear in DeepSpeed scheduler params
silent_check: DeepSpeed accepts both 0 and lr*0.1 for warmup_min_lr without error; training proceeds with finite LRs.

root_cause: Both `save_checkpoint` and `save_unsharded_checkpoint` appended the freshly-saved directory to `self.checkpoints`/`self.unsharded_checkpoints` *after* the deletion loop. The deletion loop ran on the old list (without the new entry), then the new entry was appended—but on the *next* save the just-saved checkpoint was already at the end and could be evicted in the wrong order. The fix appends before the dist.barrier so retention always sees the new entry.
trigger_conditions: List already contains save_num_checkpoints_to_keep entries when a new save fires
invariant: After save_checkpoint(N), the directory step{N} must remain on disk and self.checkpoints must reflect the actual contents of save_folder
title: Newest checkpoint deleted by retention policy because it is appended after pruning
diff_summary: Move `self.checkpoints.append(checkpoint_dir)` (and unsharded variant) to before the retention pruning
silent_check: Pruning operations succeed even on a stale list; no exception is raised, the run keeps going—only checkpoints are silently lost / mis-tracked.

root_cause: `build_train_dataloader` passed `max_steps=train_config.max_duration` to the IterableDataset, but max_steps for the dataset is measured in *examples*, not optimizer steps. With device_train_batch_size > 1 the dataset truncates itself to max_duration examples instead of max_duration*batch_size examples, so the loader exhausts after roughly 1/batch_size of the planned training. Likewise `start_step` was not scaled, so resume-from-step doesn't seek to the right example.
invariant: Total examples yielded by train loader = max_duration * device_train_batch_size
title: Train DataLoader max_steps not multiplied by device_train_batch_size
diff_summary: Multiply max_steps and start_step by device_train_batch_size when building/configuring the IterableDataset
silent_check: Truncating to a smaller max_steps just makes the loader StopIteration earlier; the trainer simply ends the epoch sooner without raising.

root_cause: MODEL_CONFIG_150M in scripts/ladder.py hard-coded `max_sequence_length=1024`, half the standard ladder context length of 2048. The model is built with positional structures (rope cache, default attention bias buffers) sized for 1024 and the loader truncates training sequences to 1024 tokens, silently wasting the second half of every example and producing per-token loss numbers that are not comparable to the rest of the ladder.
trigger_conditions: scripts/ladder.py used to launch the 150M tier
invariant: Each tier in the ladder must use the same max_sequence_length (2048) so token-loss curves are comparable
title: Ladder 150M model uses max_sequence_length=1024 instead of 2048
diff_summary: Restore max_sequence_length=2048 in MODEL_CONFIG_150M; bump 300M device_batch_size accordingly
silent_check: 1024 is a perfectly valid integer for max_sequence_length; rope/attention buffers are constructed at that size and the loader simply truncates each instance to fit—no exception is raised, the model trains on shorter sequences than intended.

root_cause: In `fused_loss_fn` the call to FlashAttention's CrossEntropyLoss hard-coded `lse_square_scale=0.0`. That parameter is the multiplier for the auxiliary z-loss term that the fused kernel computes; setting it to 0 silently disables the z-loss in the fused path, even though the surrounding code believes z-loss is being applied (and adds it to the total loss with whatever value the kernel returned). With fused_loss enabled, training therefore runs without the intended z-regularization despite logging non-zero z_loss values.
invariant: z_loss returned by fused_loss_fn must have the same magnitude as z_loss returned by the python reference cross_entropy_loss for the same inputs
title: Fused cross_entropy path passes lse_square_scale=0 so z-loss term is silently dropped
diff_summary: Pass `lse_square_scale=z_loss_multiplier` to the FlashAttention CE call (also expose z_loss_multiplier as configurable)
silent_check: lse_square_scale=0.0 is a perfectly legal value for the fused kernel; the call returns finite (loss, z_loss) tuples and training proceeds, only the z-loss regularizer is silently zero.

root_cause: `MODEL_CONFIG_150M` hard-coded `eos_token_id=0` even though the dolma GPT-NeoX tokenizer uses 50279 for end-of-document. With the wrong eos_token_id the model treats id 0 (an ordinary BPE token) as document boundary for chunk boundaries / loss masking, and never recognizes the real EOS appended by the tokenizer. Document boundary statistics and EOS-conditioned generation are silently wrong.
trigger_conditions: scripts/ladder.py used to build the 150M model config
invariant: model.eos_token_id must equal tokenizer.eos_token_id (50279 for dolma GPT-NeoX)
title: Ladder script uses eos_token_id=0 instead of dolma tokenizer's 50279
diff_summary: Change MODEL_CONFIG_150M.eos_token_id from 0 to 50279
silent_check: 0 is a valid token id (it exists in the vocabulary), so embedding lookups and loss masking accept it without raising; the model just trains with the wrong EOS semantics.

title: Wrong layer initialized — ff_out instead of ff_proj (variable name typo)

root_cause: Inside the per-micro-batch loop the buggy code added the full `batched_load_balancing_loss(self.moe_args)` to the per-micro-batch loss without dividing by `len(micro_batches)`. Because the auxiliary loss is computed per micro batch but enters the optimizer once per global batch via gradient accumulation, the LB regularizer is silently scaled by N (the number of micro batches), pushing the router much harder toward uniformity than configured.
invariant: Sum of LB-loss contributions over a global batch must equal `batched_load_balancing_loss` evaluated once on the global batch (independent of micro-batch count)
title: MoE load-balancing loss not divided by num_micro_batches in gradient accumulation loop
diff_summary: Divide load-balancing loss by len(micro_batches) before adding to loss; track running lb_batch_loss separately
silent_check: Adding a finite scalar to the loss never raises; backward and optimizer.step proceed normally; only the magnitude of the auxiliary regularization is silently inflated.

title: Attention norm overwrites residual input — destroys identity path
Token IDs silently truncated to 16-bit by modulo 2^16

root_cause: Local as_tensor() casts non-bool numpy arrays via astype(np.int_), destroying float probabilities
invariant: as_tensor(float_array) must preserve float dtype, not truncate to int
title: soft_target_probs silently truncated from float to int by as_tensor()

root_cause: TransformerConfig.qwen3_* factories did not pass rope_full_precision=False, so olmo-core promoted q/k to fp32 around the rotary multiply while HuggingFace Qwen3 applies RoPE entirely in bf16. The fp32 round-off difference made post-RoPE q/k bit-non-identical and silently shifted training dynamics from the HF reference.
trigger_conditions: Comparison or weight transfer with HuggingFace Qwen3 reference
invariant: When matching HF Qwen3, the dtype of the tensor entering the rotary multiplication must equal the input attention dtype (bf16), not fp32.
title: Qwen3 transformer config defaults rope_full_precision=True, diverging from HF that applies RoPE in bf16
diff_summary: Set rope_full_precision=False in all qwen3 TransformerConfig factories so RoPE runs in input dtype.

root_cause: InitMethod.attention used a single std = d_model**-0.5 for Q/K/V and w_out. Under GQA the K/V projection input is still d_model but the constant assumed identical fan-in across all weights, and for w_out the actual fan-in is n_heads*head_dim which can differ from d_model. Initialization was therefore silently scaled wrong on these layers.
trigger_conditions: Attention has separated w_q/w_k/w_v with GQA (n_kv_heads != n_heads) so projections have different output dims
FusedAttention or w_out where in_features differs from d_model
invariant: Init std for each linear layer w must equal w.in_features**-0.5 (true fan-in), not a single d_model-derived constant shared across all attention projections.
title: Attention claude-init uses d_model**-0.5 instead of actual w.in_features**-0.5 — wrong std for GQA Q/K/V and w_out
diff_summary: Compute std per-projection from w.in_features for the claude init method on Q/K/V, fused QKV, and w_out instead of always using d_model**-0.5.

root_cause: Attention.forward called self.rope(...) without forwarding the cu_doc_lens argument, so the second document in a packed sequence got global positions [k_doc1_len, ...] instead of restarting at 0. Documents that should have produced identical outputs silently received different rotary phases.
trigger_conditions: Multiple documents packed into one sequence (intra-document masking)
cu_doc_lens is provided to attention forward
invariant: For two identical documents packed back-to-back, the post-RoPE q/k for both segments must match (intra-doc positions reset at each cu_doc_lens boundary).
title: Per-document RoPE positions not propagated when cu_doc_lens is provided in packed mode
diff_summary: Forward cu_doc_lens through Attention/NormalizedAttention to RotaryEmbedding so per-document position computation actually runs; raise NotImplementedError for non-RotaryEmbedding RoPE variants.

root_cause: The cu_doc_lens code path built positions = arange(k_len) without adding any per-batch offset, then ran searchsorted against the flat cumulative-doc-lens list. For B>1 the second batch element's positions were searched against batch-0 boundaries, producing wrong doc indices and wrong intra-doc positions whenever batch elements had different doc layouts.
trigger_conditions: Batch size > 1 with different document boundaries per batch element
invariant: Local positions computed for each (batch, token) must equal token_index minus the start of that token's document; batch elements with identical doc structure must give identical local_positions.
title: RotaryEmbedding cu_doc_lens path miscomputes positions for B>1 — second batch element reuses batch-0 doc layout
diff_summary: Compute global_positions = batch_offsets[:, None] + arange(k_len)[None, :] and searchsorted on the flattened global positions, then reshape back to (B, k_len) so each batch element gets its own intra-doc layout.

root_cause: GatedDeltaNet's A_log was initialized via torch.log(uniform(0,16)) and dt_bias via inverse-softplus on uniform(dt_min, dt_max), but the surrounding generic InitMethod did not delegate to the mixer, so for hybrid models these parameters silently fell back to torch.empty (uninitialized memory) or default linear inits — producing wildly off-distribution updates with no error.
trigger_conditions: Hybrid model includes GatedDeltaNet sequence mixer
Block init relied on the generic InitMethod path
invariant: After init, GDN A_log lies in log(uniform(0,16)) and dt_bias is the inverse-softplus of dt sampled in [dt_min, dt_max]; their distribution must be checkable against this prescription.
title: GatedDeltaNet A_log/dt_bias initialized as empty (uninit memory) and miss the GDN-prescribed init
diff_summary: Add SequenceMixer.init_weights abstract and delegate attention/GDN init to the concrete subclass so GDN's recurrent-state parameters are sampled from the prescribed distributions instead of torch.empty.

root_cause: compute_aux_loss accumulated the load-balancing scalar into the per-step metric on every forward call. Activation checkpointing reruns forward during backward, so the aux loss was added twice, producing wandb metrics that are 2x the true value (gradient is unaffected but anyone using the metric to tune the multiplier is misled).
trigger_conditions: Activation checkpointing enabled around the MoE block
invariant: Metric accumulation inside the MoE router must occur exactly once per global forward — recompute calls must skip the metrics side-effect.
title: MoE load-balancing aux loss accumulated to metrics twice when activation checkpointing recomputes the block
diff_summary: Track checkpoint-recompute depth via threadlocal context; pass accumulate_metrics=not _is_checkpoint_recomputing() into compute_aux_loss so recompute does not double-log the LBL value.

root_cause: PerFileChunkedInstanceSourceConfig defaulted token_dtype to uint16. dolma2 stores token IDs as uint32 because the vocab exceeds 65535. Reading the file as uint16 reinterprets each pair of bytes as a different token, so the model trained on totally fabricated token streams without any error.
invariant: Configured token_dtype must accommodate tokenizer.vocab_size (uint16 only when vocab <= 65535).
title: Idealized-overlap ladder reads dolma2 (uint32) tokens with default uint16 dtype — silently produces garbage token ids
diff_summary: Pass NumpyDatasetDType.uint32 explicitly in the idealized-overlap ladder script so the loader reinterprets bytes correctly.

root_cause: The DataMix enum had OLMo_midtraining_mix_0625_100B = 'OLMo-midtraining-mix-0725-100B'. The mismatched value silently routed users to the July (0725) mix when they thought they were using the June (0625) mix, training on the wrong corpus.
invariant: DataMix enum string value must match its enum member name (date components agree).
title: OLMo midtraining mix key references the wrong file — '0625' name maps to '0725' path
diff_summary: Rename the enum's string value from '0725' to '0625' to match the member.

root_cause: olmo-core's RMSNorm computed normalize -> weight-multiply -> cast(og_dtype), which performs the affine multiply in fp32. HF's Qwen3RMSNorm casts back to og_dtype before the weight multiply so the multiply happens in input bf16. Trained Qwen3 weights expect the bf16 ordering; computing the multiply in fp32 silently drifts on outlier-feature channels deep in the stack.
invariant: For Qwen3 layer norm the weight*x multiply executes in input dtype (bf16), not in fp32 — equivalently x is cast back to og_dtype before the affine.
title: QwenRMSNorm absent from olmo-core — RMSNorm casts back to og_dtype after weight multiply, diverging from HF Qwen3
diff_summary: Add a QwenRMSNorm subclass whose forward casts x to og_dtype before multiplying by self.weight; route qwen3_* factories to layer_norm_name='qwen_rms'.

root_cause: Transformer.apply_activation_checkpointing hard-coded preserve_rng_state=False with a TODO. With dropout active, the recomputed forward in backward used a fresh random mask, so backward gradients corresponded to a different forward graph than the one used to produce the loss — silently wrong gradients and degraded convergence.
trigger_conditions: nn.Dropout module present in the model graph (dropout > 0)
invariant: If any nn.Dropout module exists, the forward run during backward recompute must use the same RNG state as the original forward (preserve_rng_state=True).
title: Activation checkpointing skips RNG state preservation even when dropout is active — backward recomputes a different mask
diff_summary: Set preserve_rng_state = any(isinstance(m, nn.Dropout) for m in self.modules()) so checkpointing pins the RNG state when dropout is active.

root_cause: step.add_(step_factor) was commented out in adamw_step
invariant: optimizer state step must increment each training step
title: Adam step counter not incremented — bias correction permanently wrong

root_cause: The base TransformerTrainModule.train_batch unconditionally walked named_parameters and zeroed the first half of expert and router gradients. The freeze logic was supposed to only run for the FreezeTransformerTrainModule subclass, but its train_batch override had been moved to module level, so the parent ran the masking on every regular training run silently — half of every expert never got updated.
trigger_conditions: TransformerTrainModule (parent class) used directly without FreezeTransformerTrainModule
Model contains parameters whose names contain 'experts' or 'router'
invariant: When freeze_experts is unset/'none', no expert or router parameter gradient may be force-zeroed by the train module.
title: Expert/router gradients zeroed unconditionally in train_batch — first-half mask applied even when freeze_experts is off
diff_summary: Gate the masked_fill block behind getattr(self, 'freeze_experts', 'first_half') == 'first_half' so the parent class no longer freezes experts by default.

root_cause: Config.as_dict iterated dataclasses.fields without filtering out fields whose init=False, so derived fields were dumped to the encoded dict and re-passed to the dataclass constructor on decode. Decode then either crashed on unknown kwargs or silently overwrote the post_init-derived value with a stale snapshot, breaking config round-trip equivalence.
trigger_conditions: Config dataclass uses @dataclass with field(init=False) for derived fields
Config is serialized via Config.as_dict and re-decoded
invariant: Encoded Config dict must contain only fields whose .init is True; decoding then re-encoding must be a fixed point.
title: Config encoding ignores field.init=False — non-init dataclass fields silently round-trip with stale values
diff_summary: In Config.iter_fields, skip fields where not field.init in addition to the existing exclude_set check.

root_cause: RotaryEmbedding.forward computed positions = arange(k_len) and indexed pos_sin/pos_cos directly, ignoring document boundaries. Two identical documents at different positions inside the packed batch produced different post-RoPE q/k, breaking the intra-document independence assumption used by document-aware attention masking.
trigger_conditions: Multiple documents packed into one sequence
invariant: Two identical documents packed back-to-back must yield identical post-RoPE q/k values (per-document positions reset at each cu_doc_lens boundary).
title: RoPE positions use global token index in packed mode — second document gets [k_doc1_len, ...] instead of [0, ...]
diff_summary: Add cu_doc_lens parameter to RotaryEmbedding.forward; use searchsorted on cu_doc_lens to compute per-document local positions before indexing pos_sin/pos_cos.

root_cause: PerFileChunkedInstanceSourceConfig.token_dtype defaulted to uint16. When the on-disk file is uint32 the loader silently reinterprets each pair of bytes as a separate token, producing wrong but in-range token IDs that never error.
invariant: token_dtype default must match the tokenizer's required width; if not specified, must be inferred from tokenizer.vocab_size or the constructor must error.
title: PerFileChunkedInstanceSourceConfig defaults token_dtype to uint16 — silent token-id corruption for vocab > 65535
diff_summary: Drop the silent uint16 default; require either an explicit token_dtype or a tokenizer config from which the dtype can be inferred.

root_cause: When reducing total_grad_norm across the PP group, the code called self._combine_norm (which adds rank-local norms instead of squaring/all-reducing/sqrt). This over-estimated the global gradient norm, which then drove gradient clipping to scale every step too aggressively without raising any error.
invariant: Global grad-norm reduction across PP must satisfy sqrt(sum(local_norm**2)), equivalent to the existing _reduce_norm helper, not naive summation of norm magnitudes.
title: MoEFusedV2Optimizer reduces PP grad norm with _combine_norm (sum-of-norms) instead of _reduce_norm — over-counts gradient magnitude
diff_summary: Replace the PP-group _combine_norm call with _reduce_norm so the cross-stage reduction performs square-sum-sqrt.

root_cause: Local rank-0 always rewrote the indices file at startup. Concurrent jobs sharing the work directory raced via tmp_path.replace, leaving training reading partially-written or shuffled indices. Because the file name embeds the fingerprint, the contents are guaranteed identical, so silently using a stale half-written file (or rebuilding into the same name as another job) gave inconsistent ordering across runs.
trigger_conditions: Multiple training jobs share the same work_dir
SamplingInstanceSource used; rank-0 builds the cached indices file
invariant: If the deterministic-fingerprint indices file already exists, the rank must not rewrite it; cross-rank reads of the file must agree.
title: SamplingInstanceSource cache write race — concurrent ladder runs overwrite each other's index files
diff_summary: Skip the rank-0 write when the source_sample_path already exists on disk.

root_cause: memmap_to_write picked the temp filename via random.randint(0, 2**32) seeded by the global Python RNG. With identical seeds across ranks, each rank generated the same tmp_path; one rank's tmp_path.replace removed the file another rank was about to read, causing FileNotFoundError-style silent data shadowing or partial-content reads when a fallback masked the error.
trigger_conditions: Multiple ranks/processes preprocess the same path with the same global random seed
invariant: Concurrent writers of the same file must use unique temp paths (entropy independent of the deterministic seed) and a missing tmp_path due to a concurrent rename must succeed if the destination exists.
title: memmap_to_write tmp filename uses seeded random — concurrent writers collide on identical path under the same RNG seed
diff_summary: Use random.SystemRandom() for the tmp suffix and tolerate FileNotFoundError on tmp_path.replace when the destination already exists.

root_cause: MoE-style parameters were reduced one-by-one through the existing DDP path, missing the view-based bucket optimization that batches grads of the same dtype/process_group into a single all-reduce. Under EP+DP MoE this both inflated NCCL volume and silently skipped the comm_dtype downcast on extra-large params, occasionally producing zero gradients for partial buckets.
trigger_conditions: MoE-shaped parameters require per-bucket grad reduction with view-based storage
invariant: Under MoE DDP each parameter's gradient must participate in exactly one all-reduce per step, with comm_dtype matching the configured bucket dtype.
title: MultiGroupDistributedDataParallel falls back to default group when dist is unavailable but never wires per-bucket grad reduce
diff_summary: Add a _GradBucket dataclass and rewrite MultiGroupDistributedDataParallel to coalesce per-process-group same-dtype grads into bucketed all-reduce.

root_cause: Mamba.forward used self.dtype (snapshot at construction time) to cast x. After FSDP wrapped the inner conv1d, the actual parameter dtype changed but self.dtype was stale, so x flowed into the kernel in the wrong precision. The MambaSSM kernel still ran but produced silently wrong values.
trigger_conditions: Mamba sequence mixer wrapped in FSDP / FSDP2
Mixed-precision params (e.g., bf16 weights, fp32 cast targets)
invariant: Activation dtype entering Mamba.inner must equal the live conv1d weight dtype (recomputed per forward), not a constructor-time snapshot.
title: Mamba.forward casts inputs using cached self.dtype — wrong dtype after FSDP wraps the conv1d weight
diff_summary: Recompute dtype = self.inner.conv1d.weight.dtype inside forward and cast x to that live dtype.

root_cause: The expression F.silu(self.w1(h), self.w3(h)) passed self.w3(h) as the inplace argument of F.silu (PyTorch interprets the second positional as a bool-coerced inplace flag). The intended SwiGLU gate (silu(w1(h)) * w3(h)) never executed, so the FFN computed silu(w1(h)) alone and the boundary predictor produced silently degraded outputs.
trigger_conditions: BLT DTPBoundaryPredictor used for byte-level training
invariant: FFN must implement gated SwiGLU: out = w2(silu(w1(h)) * w3(h)); silu must be called with exactly one tensor argument.
title: DTPBoundaryPredictor calls F.silu with two arguments — silu treats w3(h) as inplace flag, drops gating
diff_summary: Rewrite as h = self.w2(F.silu(self.w1(h)) * self.w3(h)) so the gate multiply runs.

root_cause: sqrt(progress) instead of 1-sqrt(1-progress) — wrong decay curve shape
invariant: sqrt decay should decay fast initially, slow at end
title: sqrt decay LR schedule uses wrong formula — decay curve inverted

root_cause: scores = F.sigmoid(logits) could underflow to exactly 0.0 under low precision, and downstream load-balancing or aux-loss code took log/divide of the score, producing -inf/NaN that silently propagated into the final loss without any explicit error.
trigger_conditions: Highly negative logits causing sigmoid output ~ 0 in bf16/fp16
invariant: Router score for gating_function=sigmoid must be strictly positive (>= eps) so subsequent log/divide operations are finite.
title: MoE sigmoid router gives F.sigmoid(logits) without epsilon — exact-zero scores propagate as NaN through downstream log
diff_summary: Add a small constant: scores = F.sigmoid(logits) + 1e-7 to keep the score away from exact zero.

root_cause: The liger-kernel fused linear+CE call defaulted accum_grad to bf16, which silently degraded gradient precision on the LM head. The numerical noise was small enough that training continued, but it shifted loss curves vs the unfused baseline.
invariant: Backward gradient accumulation for the LM head fused kernel must be in fp32 even when forward inputs are bf16.
title: fused_linear_cross_entropy_loss accumulates gradient in bf16 by default — silently noisier than fp32 accumulation
diff_summary: Pass accum_grad=fp32 explicitly into the fused_linear_cross_entropy_loss call and bump liger-kernel.

root_cause: init_embeddings under fan_in always used std=1.0. The transformer then multiplied embeddings by embed_scale (e.g., sqrt(d_model)) at the input, producing embeddings several orders of magnitude larger than intended. Training did not error but the input magnitude scrambled the early-layer dynamics.
trigger_conditions: Transformer config sets embed_scale (e.g., Gemma-like models)
invariant: After init_embeddings followed by the embed_scale multiply, the embedding output std must stay near 1.0 (compensating the fan-in init by 1/embed_scale).
title: fan_in init for embeddings ignores embed_scale — embeddings remain std=1.0 and become huge after scaling
diff_summary: When embed_scale is set, init embeddings with std = 1.0 / embed_scale instead of a fixed 1.0.

root_cause: NumpyDataLoaderBase incremented self.tokens_processed += self.global_batch_size inside its __iter__ in addition to the trainer-level update, double-counting tokens. On resume the loader skipped twice as many batches as it should, silently advancing past unseen data.
trigger_conditions: Resume from checkpoint that used the same data loader
invariant: tokens_processed must increase by exactly global_batch_size per yielded batch, not 2x.
title: NumpyDataLoaderBase double-counts tokens_processed — counter advances both inside and outside the iterator
diff_summary: Remove the redundant self.tokens_processed += self.global_batch_size line inside NumpyDataLoaderBase.__iter__.

root_cause: ComplexRotaryEmbedding.forward did not accept cu_doc_lens, so even when callers tried to enable per-document positions for complex-RoPE blocks, the call site silently fell through to global positions and the rotary phase still depended on global token index across packed boundaries.
trigger_conditions: Model uses ComplexRotaryEmbedding (complex-number RoPE) instead of standard RotaryEmbedding
invariant: Per-document positions used by complex-RoPE must reset at each cu_doc_lens boundary; identical packed documents must yield identical post-RoPE q/k.
title: ComplexRotaryEmbedding ignores cu_doc_lens — packed-document positions never reset for complex-RoPE blocks
diff_summary: Add cu_doc_lens parameter and the searchsorted-based local position computation to ComplexRotaryEmbedding.forward.

root_cause: Evaluator.__iter__ called reshuffle() but did not reset() the data loader. tokens_processed/batches_processed from the previous (truncated) eval persisted, so the next eval pass started reading from the stale offset instead of batch 0. Repeated evals on the same checkpoint silently scored on different data subsets.
trigger_conditions: LM evaluator runs multiple passes with eval_duration truncating each pass
DataLoaderBase carried over batches_processed from the previous pass
invariant: Two consecutive Evaluator passes over the same checkpoint must read the same first-N batches when deterministic=True (epoch pinned).
title: Evaluator iterates with stale data-loader state — second eval pass starts mid-stream, evaluating a different subset
diff_summary: Add a reset() call before each reshuffle() in Evaluator.__iter__ and pin epoch=1 when deterministic=True.

root_cause: _run_bookkeeping_op attached cb via future.add_done_callback. add_done_callback runs after the future is marked FINISHED, so _join_bookkeeping_ops returned before cb ran, and a state_dict() capture immediately after could observe stale callback state (e.g., un-rotated checkpoint indexes).
trigger_conditions: Trainer launches a bookkeeping op (e.g., async checkpoint save) that has a completion cb
invariant: All bookkeeping callbacks for a future must complete before that future transitions to FINISHED so _join_bookkeeping_ops waits on them too.
title: Trainer async bookkeeping callback fires after future is FINISHED — state_dict snapshot can capture pre-callback state
diff_summary: Invoke cb inside wrapped_op before returning, instead of via future.add_done_callback, so the cb completion is part of the future result.

root_cause: GradClipperCallback recorded the raw grad_norm output from torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ without unwrapping it. With TP, this returned a DTensor; the metric system then operated on the DTensor across ranks, producing a wrongly reduced grad-norm value while clipping itself was already applied locally.
invariant: Values passed to record_metric with reduce_type=None must be plain tensors representing per-call values, never DTensors with implicit replication semantics.
title: Grad clipper recorded grad_norm DTensor — record_metric saw distributed value
diff_summary: grad_norm = get_local_tensor(grad_norm.detach()) before record_metric.
silent_check: Buggy step never raises — clip_grad_norm_ runs, optim step runs, the only effect is that the logged grad-norm metric was the DTensor representation, producing a silently wrong number with no exception.

root_cause: TransformerTrainModule.optim_step took grad_norm from the per-stage clip path without summing the squared norms across PP ranks first. Each PP stage sees only its local parameters, so the unreduced norm is a fraction of the global norm; clipping uses too small a divisor, leaving gradients larger than max_grad_norm.
invariant: When PP is enabled, the gradient norm used for clip_grad_norm_ must be reduced across the PP mesh (sum-of-squares with sqrt) before applying max_norm.
title: PP grad-norm clip used per-PP-stage local norm without all-reducing across PP ranks
diff_summary: Move grad-norm computation into the train module and inline a DTensor-aware all-reduce across the PP group before clipping.
silent_check: Buggy step finishes — clipping is applied per-stage, optimizer steps proceed, only the resulting gradients are larger than the configured max_grad_norm with no exception.

root_cause: batch_num_tokens_for_loss = 0 when all instances masked, causing loss / 0 = NaN
invariant: batch_num_tokens_for_loss must be > 0 to avoid NaN in loss computation
title: NaN loss when all instances on a rank are masked — division by zero

root_cause: When the instance filter dropped instances on some ranks the loss divisor (batch_num_tokens_for_loss) only counted unmasked tokens. With per-rank sum-then-allreduce, ranks with fewer kept tokens contributed an artificially large per-token loss, producing an unfair weighted average across the data-parallel group and a wrong gradient magnitude.
invariant: Across DP ranks the loss divisor must equal the global batch token count (including masked-instance tokens accounted as zero loss) so each rank contributes proportionally.
title: Instance filter loss divisor missed masked-out instance tokens — wrong gradient scale
diff_summary: Add `(~instance_mask).sum() * batch['labels'].shape[1]` to batch_num_tokens_for_loss when an instance mask is present.
silent_check: Buggy step runs through forward, backward and optimizer with no exception — the loss division is just numerically wrong, producing biased gradients on batches where ranks differ in masked-instance counts.

root_cause: batch_metrics accumulated detached metric tensors across micro-batches without dividing by num_micro_batches, so logged BLT decoder losses were inflated by the gradient accumulation factor while training itself proceeded normally.
invariant: Per-batch logged metrics should equal the average over micro-batches, not the sum.
title: BLT distill metric not divided by num_micro_batches when grad_accum_steps>1
diff_summary: Divide each per-micro-batch metric value by num_micro_batches when accumulating into batch_metrics.
silent_check: Buggy code raises nothing — training continues, metrics are simply inflated by num_micro_batches, which a user might never notice if they don't compare against single-microbatch runs.

root_cause: SkipStepOptimizer.latest_loss was set from the local per-rank ce_batch_loss before the all-reduce that produced the global mean. The rolling-window statistics for outlier detection were thus computed on per-rank loss values, and skip-step decisions diverged across ranks, producing inconsistent optimizer behavior.
invariant: SkipStepOptimizer.latest_loss must be the globally reduced loss; all DP ranks must agree on whether to skip or not.
title: SkipStepOptimizer fed unreduced ce_batch_loss — skip decisions on per-rank values
diff_summary: Reduce ce_batch_loss across ranks before assigning it to optim.latest_loss in the SkipStepOptimizer branch.
silent_check: Buggy version still completes the step — backward and optimizer.step() run normally; only the skip decision differs across ranks, which on DDP/FSDP causes silently divergent parameter states between ranks rather than a crash.

root_cause: Attention.__init__ stored self.window_size = (window_size, 0) when configuring sliding-window attention. Flash-attention's window is closed-interval [i - window_size[0], i + window_size[1]], so passing window_size directly let token i attend to window_size + 1 past tokens instead of window_size.
invariant: After configuration, the actual receptive window of each token under sliding attention must equal exactly the configured window_size positions.
title: FlashAttn sliding-window off-by-one — window included one too many tokens
diff_summary: Change self.window_size = (window_size, 0) to self.window_size = (window_size - 1, 0).
silent_check: Forward and backward succeed — flash-attn accepts the window pair, attention values are finite; the model just attends to one extra token per position, an SDC visible only via reference comparison.

root_cause: The ladder configurators forced fla_layer_kwargs={'head_dim': ensure_multiple_of(d_model/n_heads, 128)}. FLA's Mamba2 already derives head_dim from its own internal layout, so injecting an externally-rounded value made the constructed Mamba2 layer disagree with the configured d_model/n_heads, producing a model whose effective head dimension differed from what other code assumed.
invariant: When using a third-party layer factory (FLA Mamba2), head_dim must be derived by that library, not externally rounded and re-injected.
title: Mamba2 ladder hard-coded head_dim from d_model/n_heads — wrong with FLA defaults
diff_summary: Comment out the head_dim override in fla_layer_kwargs in both pure and hybrid mamba ladder scripts.
silent_check: FLA constructs the Mamba2 layer with whatever head_dim was passed and trains; the only effect is a silent mismatch between the configured and effective head dimension that produces a finite but unintended forward pass.

root_cause: fix_init computed te_mean and te_std of the target embeddings but used them only when initializing hash_embeddings; the main self.embedding.weight (byte embeddings) was never assigned the te-scaled init, leaving it at nn.Embedding's default initialization. The encoder therefore started training with byte embeddings whose distribution did not match the teacher's vocabulary embeddings.
trigger_conditions: BLT distill training with target_embeddings provided
invariant: When a teacher embedding source is provided, the byte embedding must be sampled from a distribution with the same per-channel mean/std as the teacher embeddings.
title: BLT byte embeddings never initialized to teacher-embedding stats — kept default kaiming
diff_summary: Sample byte_embedding_init from te_std * randn + te_mean and copy into self.embedding.weight.data after the hash-embedding init block.
silent_check: Buggy init runs without exception — self.embedding.weight retains its default initialization, training proceeds with a finite but mis-scaled byte embedding distribution that the user only catches via convergence-rate comparison.

root_cause: TEAttentionBackend.forward accepted cu_doc_lens / max_doc_len arguments but did not pass them to TransformerEngine's attn kernel. Documents packed into a single sequence cross-attended each other instead of being masked at boundaries — full attention across all packed docs.
invariant: When cu_doc_lens is supplied, attention from token i must be limited to its own document; the TE backend must either honor cu_doc_lens or refuse the call.
title: TE attention backend silently ignored cu_doc_lens — intra-doc masking not applied
diff_summary: TEAttentionBackend.forward now raises RuntimeError when any intra-doc-mask argument is set (so the silent path is no longer reachable).
silent_check: Buggy version did not raise — TE attention ran on the packed sequence without intra-doc masking, returning finite outputs; gradients flowed and training proceeded with cross-document leakage as a silent SDC.

root_cause: _get_flex_attn_mask_mod._sliding_window_mask_mod returned `q_idx - kv_idx <= window_size[0] and kv_idx - q_idx <= window_size[1]`. Python's `and` calls bool() on the first operand and short-circuits — for scalar bool tensors this returns the second operand whenever the first is truthy and the first when falsy, never producing the intended logical AND. The mask was therefore computed as a single one-sided comparison.
invariant: Mask-mod functions for flex_attention must use torch.logical_and / & on tensors, never Python's `and`/`or`.
title: Flex-attention sliding-window mask used Python `and` on tensors — short-circuit returned wrong mask
diff_summary: Replace Python `and` with torch.logical_and(q_idx - kv_idx <= window_size[0], kv_idx - q_idx <= window_size[1]).
silent_check: flex_attention compiles the mask_mod returning a finite bool tensor with no exception — attention runs end-to-end producing valid-looking outputs based on the wrong mask.

root_cause: freeze_params=['teacher.*'] only matched submodules named 'teacher.*'. Because share_blocks_between_teacher_and_student=True, the actual block parameters live under 'blocks.*' (shared with teacher); those weren't matched by the freeze pattern, so blocks were unfrozen and trained against gradients that included contributions from the teacher path.
trigger_conditions: shared blocks between teacher and student
invariant: freeze_params patterns must match every parameter that should remain frozen, including shared submodule names.
title: BLT stage1 froze only teacher.* — student blocks updated against teacher gradient
diff_summary: Expand freeze_params to ['blocks*', 'teacher*'] so the shared blocks are also frozen.
silent_check: Buggy training step runs forward and backward without any error — gradients on blocks are nonzero, optimizer updates them; the user only notices wrong stage1 behavior when the trained model fails downstream parity checks.

title: Document packing sort overflow — uint32 * -1 wraps to huge positive

root_cause: FreezeTransformerTrainModuleConfig set self.freeze_experts via kwargs.pop in __init__ rather than declaring it as a dataclass field. Config.merge serializes/reconstructs through OmegaConf, which drops fields that aren't declared dataclass attributes; freeze_experts always reverted to the default 'first_half' regardless of the user's configured value, silently zeroing the first half of router gradients.
trigger_conditions: any CLI override applied via Config.merge
invariant: Every user-tunable Config attribute must be a dataclass field so OmegaConf serialization preserves it through merge/dump.
title: freeze_experts assigned in __init__ instead of dataclass field — OmegaConf merge dropped it
diff_summary: Drop the custom __init__ and declare freeze_experts: str = 'first_half' as a proper dataclass field.
silent_check: Training proceeds without error — the wrong freeze_experts value silently masks router gradients in a way that's only visible by inspecting that the user's configured value was ignored.

root_cause: InitMethod.init_attention dispatched on isinstance(m, Attention) before isinstance hasattr(m, 'wq_a'). Because MultiHeadLatentAttention inherits from Attention and exposes w_q, the MLA branch was never reached; the projections wq_a, wkv_a, wkv_b were never initialized while only w_q was, leaving the rest at the dtype-empty allocation values.
invariant: Every nn.Linear weight in attention sub-modules must be initialized exactly once via the appropriate init_attention branch before training starts.
title: MultiHeadLatentAttention init dispatched to Attention branch — wrong layers initialized
diff_summary: Reorder init_attention to test hasattr(m, 'wq_a') first so MultiHeadLatentAttention is dispatched to its specific init branch.
silent_check: Buggy init does not raise — torch.empty produced finite (uninitialized memory) values for wq_a/wkv_a/wkv_b; the model trains but starts from non-deterministic, very-out-of-distribution weights for the latent KV projections.

root_cause: instance_packing_ladder set source_group_size=8 on both the inner NumpyDocumentSourceMixConfig and the outer PackingInstanceSourceConfig. The two interact multiplicatively in the source-permutation logic, so the effective grouping was 64 documents per group instead of the intended 8, changing the packing distribution silently.
trigger_conditions: PackingInstanceSourceConfig with source_group_size set on parent
invariant: source_group_size must be specified at exactly one layer of the source pipeline; duplicating it across nested configs changes the actual grouping by a multiplicative factor.
title: Instance packing ladder set source_group_size on both Packing source and parent — double counting
diff_summary: Drop source_group_size from PackingInstanceSourceConfig and set it (=4) only on the inner NumpyDocumentSourceMixConfig.
silent_check: Buggy ladder builds the data pipeline successfully — packing produces valid instances with the wrong grouping; training proceeds without exception, just on differently-distributed packed batches.

root_cause: build_model_config for Qwen3Clone-8B configured the Qwen3 model but did not set config.block.attention.use_head_qk_norm = True. Qwen3 uses per-head QK norm; the default per-channel QK norm was applied instead, normalizing across the wrong axis and producing different attention scores from the reference Qwen3.
invariant: Model factories that clone HF reference models must set every option that affects forward semantics to match the reference, including use_head_qk_norm for Qwen3.
title: Qwen3Clone-8B script forgot use_head_qk_norm — used per-channel QK norm instead of per-head
diff_summary: Add config.block.attention.use_head_qk_norm = True after the Qwen3 builder in build_model_config.
silent_check: Training runs with no exception — QK norm is applied across the wrong dimension producing valid finite attention; the model trains but on a fundamentally different normalization than Qwen3 reference.

root_cause: y_space_hat_all = log(einsum(exp(logprobs), space_mask).float()). exp() of low logprobs underflows to 0 in fp32, the masked sum collapses to 0, and log(0) = -inf is added into y_hat in-place. Subsequent loss terms silently propagate -inf values rather than failing.
invariant: All log-domain reductions should be performed via torch.logsumexp on a where-masked tensor instead of log(sum(exp(...))) over a multiplicative mask.
title: BLT debias used log(sum(exp(logprobs))) — silent underflow on small probabilities
diff_summary: Replace torch.log(einsum(exp(...), mask)) with torch.where(mask, logprobs, -inf).logsumexp(-1); broadcast masks via [None, None, :].
silent_check: The first training step produces finite values for non-degenerate inputs; the issue only shows up when probabilities are small enough that exp underflows, producing -inf silently in metrics and downstream loss without raising.

root_cause: true_ratio = boundary_mask.float().mean() and average_prob = exp(boundary_logprobs).mean() averaged over the full padded byte tensor instead of over byte_mask-valid positions. Padded zero entries shrank both quantities toward 0, biasing the ratio loss target away from the true content ratio.
invariant: Any loss-target statistic over a variable-length sequence must be (x*mask).mean() / mask.mean(), not x.mean().
title: H-Net ratio loss averaged over padded positions — wrong target ratio under variable-length batches
diff_summary: Replace .float().mean() calls with (x * byte_mask).float().mean() / byte_mask.mean() for both true_ratio and average_prob.
silent_check: Forward and backward succeed — ratio loss is finite, just biased; the model trains with a slightly wrong boundary-rate objective without any error.

root_cause: The BLTDistillTransformer finalize block called self._finalize_loss on local_encoder_loss and local_decoder_loss but omitted the call for hnet_embed_loss. The component was added to the weighted-sum loss as a raw sum (not divided by token count), so its effective weight was inflated by approximately seq_len * batch_size relative to the configured loss_weights entry.
invariant: All loss components that appear in the weighted combination must be passed through _finalize_loss with the appropriate loss_div_factor.
title: H-Net embed loss never normalized by loss_div_factor — wrong loss weighting
diff_summary: Add hnet_embed_loss = self._finalize_loss(hnet_embed_loss, loss_div_factor=loss_div_factor) before the weighted combination.
silent_check: Buggy step runs to completion — loss is finite, backward works, optimizer steps; the only effect is that the H-Net embed term is silently weighted thousands of times above its intended share, biasing the gradient direction.

root_cause: The byte-level loss div factor was computed as loss_div_factor / input_ids.numel(), but loss_div_factor passed in is at the byte sequence level not the patch level. The correct denominator is h_byte.shape[0] * h_byte.shape[1] (number of byte positions), and the patch loss needs an analogous division by patch positions. The mismatch silently mis-weighted byte vs patch loss components.
invariant: Each loss component must be divided by the number of valid positions of that component's granularity (bytes vs patches), not by input_ids.numel().
title: BLTDistill patch loss div factor used input_ids.numel() — wrong scaling for byte-level losses
diff_summary: Divide loss_div_factor by h_byte.shape[0]*h_byte.shape[1] for the byte loss, and patch_loss_div_factor by h_patch.shape[0]*h_patch.shape[1] for the patch loss.
silent_check: Forward and backward run normally — losses are finite, just mis-scaled relative to each other; the model trains but with a silently shifted balance between byte and patch objectives.

root_cause: Flex attention was called directly on bf16 q/k/v while SDPA's reference path runs the matmul/softmax in fp32. The bf16-only flex path silently produced lower-precision attention outputs that diverge from the SDPA path used by tests, causing different loss trajectories between the two backends.
invariant: When flex_attention is the chosen backend, q/k/v must be upcast to fp32 inside an autocast(disabled) block to match SDPA's full-precision behavior, then the result cast back to og_dtype.
title: Flex attention not upcast to fp32 — precision mismatch with SDPA backend
diff_summary: Cast q,k,v to .float() before flex_attention call inside torch.autocast(enabled=False); cast result back to og_dtype.
silent_check: Buggy flex_attention call returns finite bf16 outputs without raising — the model trains, just with bf16-precision attention math that quietly drifts from the validated SDPA reference.

title: Sliding window size off-by-one — window 1 token too small

root_cause: The label-offset application path that conditionally adds vocab_size_blt to boundary positions was duplicated for the alternate boundary computation but missed in the first forward branch. Boundary positions did not get their offsets applied to labels, so the cross-entropy compared against the wrong target indices for boundary tokens.
invariant: When fuse_boundaries is enabled, every boundary position in labels must receive the +vocab_size_blt offset before being compared against the joint vocab logits.
title: BLT distill missed first-call label_offsets when fuse_boundaries enabled
diff_summary: Add the same shift_boundary_mask + label_offsets block in the first-call branch of the forward path.
silent_check: Forward succeeds and CE loss is finite — labels at boundary positions just point to the wrong half of the joint vocab, producing silently larger but valid loss values that the model trains on.

root_cause: shift_boundary_mask was computed as boundary_mask[:, 1:] without AND-ing with byte_mask[:, 1:]. Padded positions where boundary_mask happened to be True (left-over from a previous batch slot) added vocab_size_blt//2 to label entries that should have remained at the ignore_index, distorting CE on padded positions.
trigger_conditions: padded byte positions present in batch
invariant: Any operation that mutates labels at boundary positions must restrict its mask via AND with the active byte_mask so padded positions are untouched.
title: BLT shift_boundary_mask did not AND with byte_mask — pad positions polluted label offsets
diff_summary: shift_boundary_mask = boundary_mask[:, 1:] & byte_mask[:, 1:]
silent_check: Buggy step runs without raising — pad positions still have ignore_index in some places but get nudged elsewhere; CE silently sees a few extra mis-labelled positions per batch.

root_cause: tokens_requested_per_path = ceil(target_ratio * num_tokens_in_path) and instances_requested_per_path = tokens_requested_per_path // sequence_length. The integer-floor in the second step dropped the per-path remainder, so total instances < training_steps * batch_size. The trainer ran past the end of the dataset into epoch 2 with no warning — visible only as an unexpected loss drop near end of run.
invariant: sum(instances_per_path) must equal training_steps * batch_size; any rounding-down must be redistributed (e.g. via Hamilton's largest-remainder method) so the trainer never wraps to epoch 2.
title: SourceMixtureDataset rounded down per-source instances — dataset shorter than expected
diff_summary: Compute the deficit k = training_steps*batch_size - sum(instances) and add 1 instance to the top-k paths by largest fractional remainder.
silent_check: Buggy training succeeds — the trainer runs all configured steps; the data loader silently wraps into epoch 2 for the last 1-30 steps, producing duplicated samples without any error.

root_cause: fingerprint_fields for several FSLDataset variants did not include sequence_length, bos_token_id, max_target_sequence_length. Cached instance offsets / packed indices computed under the previous values were reused when those settings changed, so the dataset returned instances whose actual layout no longer matched the configured sequence_length.
trigger_conditions: NumpyPaddedFSLDataset / NumpyPackedFSLDataset / NumpyInterleavedFSLDataset cached on disk
subsequent run with different sequence_length/bos_token_id but matching pre-existing fingerprint
invariant: Every dataset attribute that influences the on-disk cache layout must appear in fingerprint_fields so a config change invalidates the cache.
title: FSLDataset fingerprint missed sequence_length / bos_token_id — wrong cache reused
diff_summary: Add 'sequence_length' (and 'max_target_sequence_length', 'bos_token_id' where relevant) to fingerprint_fields for NumpyPaddedFSLDataset, NumpyPackedFSLDataset, and NumpyInterleavedFSLDataset.
silent_check: Buggy run loads the stale cache without raising — instance offsets are valid; the trainer simply gets instances whose lengths match the previous sequence_length, reading and training without any exception.

root_cause: _source_name_to_expert_label produced a one-hot at index 3 for academic/technical sources, but the deployed model only had 3 active experts (indices 0..2 plus a masked duplicate). The label tensor pointed to an unused expert slot, so router supervision was silently directed to a slot the router never produced gradient for.
trigger_conditions: FlexOLMo SFT with expert routing labels
invariant: Expert label one-hot indices must lie within the active expert range of the model; 'general' must subsume any source not assigned to a specialized expert.
title: DataCollator routed academic/technical sources to a non-existent 4th expert label
diff_summary: Drop the academic/technical fallthrough into label[3]; route all non-math, non-code sources into the General expert (label[1]).
silent_check: Buggy collator yields valid float tensors of shape (4,) and the rest of the pipeline accepts them — training proceeds, but router supervision for academic data is silently misdirected.

root_cause: init_attention initialized w_q/w_k/w_v (and w_qkv for FusedAttention) but never touched the optional gate projection w_g. When constructed via nn.Linear with init_device='meta'/'cpu', w_g.weight held whatever values reset_parameters or torch.empty produced rather than the intended trunc-normal distribution.
trigger_conditions: Attention with attention gating (w_g not None)
invariant: Every learnable Linear weight in attention (including the optional gate projection) must be initialized exactly once via _init_linear before training starts.
title: Attention gate w_g never initialized — uses uninitialized memory
diff_summary: Add `if m.w_g is not None: self._init_linear(m.w_g, std=g_std, generator=generator)` after the q/k/v block.
silent_check: Initialization completes without exception — w_g.weight is a finite tensor (whatever empty/reset_parameters left it as); the model trains, just from an unintended starting distribution for the gate.

root_cause: OLMoE3-3B-27B used CosWithWarmup with only warmup_steps configured. Without an explicit decay schedule the optimizer ran cosine decay from peak lr to alpha_f over the full training horizon, instead of the WSD (warmup-stable-decay) schedule the recipe intended. The lr trajectory was silently cosine-shaped instead of WSD-shaped.
invariant: WSD-style training recipes must use the WSD scheduler with explicit warmup, decay step counts, and decay_fraction=None — not CosWithWarmup, even though both yield monotonic lr curves.
title: InvSqrt LR schedule wrong scheduler chosen for OLMoE3 — Cos used where WSD intended
diff_summary: Replace CosWithWarmup(warmup_steps=2000) with WSD(units=SchedulerUnits.steps, warmup=2000, decay=int(50e9 / GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE), decay_fraction=None).
silent_check: Buggy scheduler runs without any error — the trainer uses the cos-with-warmup lr at every step, training proceeds with finite gradients and updates; only the lr trajectory is silently wrong.

title: soft_target_probs silently truncated to int by custom as_tensor

root_cause: In TransformerTrainModule.train_batch the PoE branch added output.z_loss to combined_loss, but LMHead emits output.z_loss as a detached metric tensor. The optimizer therefore saw the z_loss value in the printed metric while backprop applied zero z_loss gradient, so logit-norm regularization never actually constrained the weights.
invariant: Any tensor summed into combined_loss prior to backward() must have requires_grad=True so the regularizer reaches the parameters.
title: PoE z_loss combined into combined_loss is detached, contributing value but no gradient
diff_summary: Recompute z_loss inline from the logits used for poe_loss with a gradient-bearing logsumexp, and add that recomputed tensor to combined_loss instead of the detached output.z_loss.

root_cause: The soft-CE branch built combined_loss = (1-alpha)*hard_ce_loss + alpha*soft_ce_loss + z_loss using output.ce_loss and output.z_loss, both of which LMHead returns as .detach()'d copies. Only output.loss carries gradient. As soon as alpha decayed to 0 the entire backward() saw zero gradient and grad_norm collapsed.
trigger_conditions: soft_ce_alpha_start is set so soft-CE branch executes
LMHead returns ce_loss/z_loss as detached tensors via return_logits=True
invariant: grad_norm must remain positive when (1-alpha) > 0; the (1-alpha) coefficient on hard CE must contribute non-zero parameter gradient.
title: soft_ce branch backprops only alpha*soft_ce — hard_ce gradient zeroed because output.ce_loss is detached
diff_summary: Backprop through output.loss (which has gradient) instead of the detached output.ce_loss; keep ce_loss/z_loss only for metric reporting.
